fabricroadmap.title: Power Query - Modern Power Query Editor in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI Desktop will adopt the Modern Power Query Editor, bringing next‑generation authoring, usability, and productivity enhancements that are not available in the legacy Power Query experience. This modern editor aligns Power BI Desktop with the latest Power Query innovations used across Fabric, Dataflows, Power BI Web Modeling and other Power Query Online integrations, and serves as the foundation for ongoing transformation UX improvements.The modern editor introduces a set of authoring‑centric capabilities designed to make complex queries easier to build, understand, and maintain—especial

fabricroadmap.title: dbt job - Support for dbt Fusion runtime in dbt job
fabricroadmap.summary: We are adding support dbt Fusion runtime in dbt job in Microsoft Fabric as an execution environment, in addition to the existing dbt Core–based runtime.Customers can select the Fusion runtime when creating or configuring a dbt job to run their transformations on the next-generation dbt engine — natively inside Fabric, with no local tooling or external orchestration to manage.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Shared Queries
fabricroadmap.summary: Shared Queries in Dataflow Gen2 will be available in Preview, enabling users to save commonly used Power Query transformations within a Fabric workspace, share and reuse them across multiple dataflows and collaborators.This preview extends the reuse‑first authoring model to teams, making it easy to apply trusted, reusable logic—such as data cleansing steps, business rules, or standard joins—consistently across projects without rebuilding queries from scratch.Key benefits and scenarios: Share common transformation logic across workspace members to accelerate team-wide development Promote consis

fabricroadmap.title: GA AutoML in Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) enables users to build and deploy machine learning models by automating the most time-consuming and complex parts of the model development process. The General Availability will enable users to simplofy the ML development cycle by using AutoML to automatically select the best algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and generate optimized models based on the input data and desired outcomes.

fabricroadmap.title: Machine Learning Model Endpoint Monitoring
fabricroadmap.summary: After activating ML Model endpoints in Fabric, users will need to monitor the quality of their models and the health of their endpoints in the artifact UI with a corresponding set of dynamic graphs. With this feature released, users are able to see request rate, request error rate, and latency on ML model endpoint monitoring UI.

fabricroadmap.title: Support AutoML with FLAML in ML model endpoints
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables users to deploy models with internal dependencies, such as AutoML or FLAML, directly through ML model endpoints.

fabricroadmap.title: CI/CD for Models and Experiments
fabricroadmap.summary: The Machine learning experiments and models integrate with the lifecycle management capabilities in Microsoft Fabric, providing a standardized collaboration between all development team members throughout the product's life. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-science/machine-learning-artifacts-git-deployment-pipelines

fabricroadmap.title: AI Functions for LLM-Powered Text Enrichment and Transformation [GA]
fabricroadmap.summary: AI functions in Fabric will allow notebook users to seamlessly perform tasks like text summarization, translation, classification, sentiment analysis, grammar correction, and more, providing a simplified API for common enrichments and making it easier for users to apply them with fewer lines of code. The functions will be initially available on top of pandas DataFrames and ultimately available via Spark, SQL, and other programming surfaces across Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: Low-Code AI-Powered Operations in Data Wrangler [GA]
fabricroadmap.summary: A new suite of AI-powered operations in Data Wrangler will allow users to describe code transformations with natural language and generate the corresponding Python; translate custom Python code into PySpark code; and view high-confidence suggestions for operations based on their working data.

fabricroadmap.title: Multimodal Support for AI Functions [Public Preview]
fabricroadmap.summary: Multimodal support for AI functions in Fabric will allow notebook users to use AI functions on their unstructured data in pdf, image, and text file formats, to seamlessly perform tasks like summarization, classification, sentiment analysis, and more, with just a few lines of code. The multimodal support for AI functions will be available with both pandas and Spark.

fabricroadmap.title: Service Principal authentication supported in Semantic Link
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature adds Azure service principal (SPN) support as an authentication type for Semantic Link.An Azure service principal is a non-human security identity used by applications or automation tools to access Azure resources with precise permissions.Using service principals in Semantic Link allows Power BI admins to manage and optimize Fabric items securely and efficiently, without relying on user identities.

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time Endpoints for Machine Learning Models [Public Preview]
fabricroadmap.summary: Alongside the existing functionality for batch scoring with PREDICT, Fabric will allow data scientists to serve real-time predictions from any registered ML Model using secure, scalable online endpoints that are automatically configured. These endpoints can be called from other Fabric engines or from external apps, allowing users to deploy their models for wide, reliable consumption.

fabricroadmap.title: AI functions in Data Wrangler [Public Preview]
fabricroadmap.summary: AI functions in Data Wrangler will allow users to enrich and transform data directly within the Data Wrangler interface. With just a few clicks, users can perform tasks such as text summarization, translation, classification, sentiment analysis, grammar correction, and more, streamlining data preparation through seamless, built-in AI capabilities.

fabricroadmap.title: AI Functions for LLM-Powered Text Enrichment and Transformation [Public Preview]
fabricroadmap.summary: AI functions in Fabric will allow notebook users to seamlessly perform tasks like text summarization, translation, classification, sentiment analysis, grammar correction, and more, providing a simplified API for common enrichments and making it easier for users to apply them with fewer lines of code. The functions will be initially available on top of pandas DataFrames and ultimately available via Spark, SQL, and other programming surfaces across Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: Low Code AutoML
fabricroadmap.summary: Our Low-Code AutoML tool empowers data scientists and analysts to easily create machine learning models without the need for extensive coding. Through an intuitive, step-by-step wizard, users can configure and launch AutoML trials directly from the user interface.

fabricroadmap.title: Feature Store
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric feature store is a centralized system that manages the data inputs, called features, that power machine learning models. It bridges raw data and ML models, giving teams one place to define, store, serve, and discover features instead of each team building its own pipelines.

fabricroadmap.title: MLOps: model alias
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature is to offer a model alias that provides a stable, human‑readable name pointing to a specific model version. This lets them switch, promote, or roll back model versions safely without breaking downstream integrations.

fabricroadmap.title: Support tensor based models on model endpoints
fabricroadmap.summary: ML Endpoints are currently available for a limited set of ML model flavors, including Keras, LightGBM, Sklearn, and XGBoost. This feature allows users to activate ML endpoints for models with tensor-based schemas or no schemas.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for ML Experiment
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allow fabric enterprise customers to use ML experiments in Outbound Access Protection enabled workspace and prevent sensitive data from getting exfiltrated.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for ML Model
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables Fabric enterprise customers to use ML models in Outbound Access Protection (OAP) enabled workspace and prevent sensitive data from getting exfiltrated.

fabricroadmap.title: MLFlow 3 in Fabric : logged model and traces
fabricroadmap.summary: MLflow 3 arrives in Fabric with support for tracing, logged models, and an upgraded experiment tracking UX. The update introduces a new trace table view and nested trace visualization for inspecting multi-step model execution paths, a dedicated trace detail page, and the logged model API and UX for capturing and managing model artifacts as first-class objects. Together, these provide a more structured workflow for tracking experiments, registering models, and understanding model behavior.

fabricroadmap.title: GA foundry tools in Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: Formerly named Azure Cognitive Services, Foundry Tools on Fabric brings in Azure Language, Azure Translator, and Azure Content Understanding as native endpoints for both Fabric workload teams and end users. With these endpoints, Fabric workload teams and end users can build intelligent solutions without having AI or data science expertise.

fabricroadmap.title: External data sources
fabricroadmap.summary: The EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE feature allows you to define a root URI that can be referenced by name in OPENROWSET and BULK INSERT operations. By using the DATA SOURCE option, you can reference files using relative paths, eliminating the need to specify long absolute URIs.

fabricroadmap.title: Detection and reuse of common subexpression
fabricroadmap.summary: Within an inflight query execution, detect common subexpression and reuse its results for executing other parts of the same query.

fabricroadmap.summary: The OPENROWSET(BULK) function allows you to query external data (such as CSV and Parquet files) stored in the lake using the T-SQL syntax. fabricroadmap.title: Regular expressions
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Data Warehouse will introduce T-SQL functions for pattern matching, text extraction, and transformation using regular expressions. These capabilities will make it easier to validate, search, and manipulate text data directly within your queries.New functions include: REGEXP\_LIKE – Returns a Boolean indicating if the text matches the regex pattern. fabricroadmap.title: Live connectivity to source for migration to Fabric Data Warehouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Migration Assistant for Fabric Data Warehouse will support live connection to Azure Synapse Analytics Dedicated SQL Pool to bring metadata objects from the source system to Fabric Data Warehouse. With this release, users will also be able to select objects to migrate from the source system.

fabricroadmap.title: Offline migration with SQL database project file
fabricroadmap.summary: Migration Assistant for Fabric Data Warehouse will support SQL database project file along with DACPAC file format to migrate from the source system like Azure Synapse Analytics to Fabric Data Warehouse.

fabricroadmap.title: Fuzzy string matching
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Data Warehouse will introduce string similarity and comparison functions based on Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler algorithms. fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Data Warehouse will introduce the ANY_VALUE() function.<br/>This function returns a value from a column within each group when all values in that group are the same, without requiring explicit aggregation logic like MIN() or MAX().<br/>It’s ideal for scenarios where grouped columns contain identical values, and you simply need one of them for reporting or joining purposes.This makes queries cleaner and easier to write while preserving performance and correctness.<br/> ```SELECT c.CustomerID, ANY_VALUE(c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName) AS CustomerName, ANY_VALUE(c.Company

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcuts in Fabric Data Warehouse (Public Preview)
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcuts in Fabric DW allow users to directly access and query data that is present in internal and external data sources, without loading them into Fabric DW. Users will have the capability to create Table Shortcuts via TSQL & UX

fabricroadmap.title: SQL Audit Logs Improvments
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature will introduce enhancements to SQL Audit Logs, including support for audit event filtering and query size enforcement.These capabilities help customers reduce audit noise and improve audit completeness by controlling which events are captured and preventing oversized queries from exceeding audit limits.

fabricroadmap.title: COPY INTO & OPENROWSET support from OneLake

fabricroadmap.summary: Using the built-in warehouse monitoring experience, you can view both live queries and historical queries, monitor, and troubleshoot performance of their end-to-end solution.

fabricroadmap.title: Get Warehouse Schema Rest API
fabricroadmap.summary: The REST API allows users to export the full warehouse definition, including schemas, tables, views, functions, and stored procedures, with filtering options to support exporting a subset of the warehouse definition.

fabricroadmap.title: Case insensitive collation support (Warehouse only)
fabricroadmap.summary: Using the public REST APIs to create a Data Warehouse includes a new option to set the default collation. This can be used to set a new Case Insensitive Collation default. The two supported collations are Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_KS_WS_SC_UTF8 (which is Case Insensitive) and Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8 (which is Case Sensitive) and continues to be our default. COLLATE T-SQL clause support is coming soon. This will enable you to utilize the COLLATE command with CREATE or ALTER TABLE to directly specify the collation for your VARCHAR fields.

fabricroadmap.title: ALTER TABLE - Add nullable column
fabricroadmap.summary: Support for ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN to be able to extend already existing tables with new columns that allow NULL values.

fabricroadmap.title: TRUNCATE
fabricroadmap.summary: The TRUNCATE command quickly removes all rows of data from a table.

fabricroadmap.title: Incremental Statistics Refresh
fabricroadmap.summary: Incremental Statistics Refresh is a performance optimization to automatic statistic updates. It opportunistically reduces duration of automatic statistic updates by only sampling newly-added rows (instead of the entire column), thereby speeding up user queries that must update statistics before running.

fabricroadmap.title: SQL Pool Insights
fabricroadmap.summary: The sql_pool_insights view in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse provides actionable insights into the configuration and utilization of SQL pools via Query Insights. It helps users monitor resource allocation, track configuration changes, and identify periods when pools are under pressure. This enables data engineers and administrators to optimize workloads and troubleshoot performance issues efficiently.

fabricroadmap.title: Nested CTE
fabricroadmap.summary: Common Table Expressions (CTE) increases the readability and simplification for complex queries by deconstructing ordinarily complex queries into simple blocks to be used and reused if necessary, instead of rewriting the query. A nested CTE is defined with the definition of another CTE.

fabricroadmap.title: Time travel
fabricroadmap.summary: The ability to time travel at the T-SQL statement level empowers users to query historical data from various past timeframes by specifying the timestamp only once for the entire query. Time travel helps save significantly on storage costs by using single copy of data present in One Lake for conducting historical trend analysis, troubleshooting, and data reconciliation. Additionally, it also facilitates achieving stable reporting by upholding the data integrity across various tables within the data warehouse.

fabricroadmap.title: In-place restore within warehouse editor
fabricroadmap.summary: You can now easily create restore points and restore the warehouse to a known good state in the event of accidental corruption, using the Warehouse editor experience.

fabricroadmap.title: COPY INTO support for secure storage
fabricroadmap.summary: You can now ingest data into your Warehouse using COPY INTO from an external Azure storage account that is protected behind a Firewall.

fabricroadmap.title: T-SQL Notebook integration
fabricroadmap.summary: You can start using T-SQL language support within Notebooks which combines the power of Notebooks and SQL within the same experience - enabling intellisense, autocomplete, cross database queries, richer visualizations and the ability to easily collaborate and share using Notebooks.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot enables developers of any skill level to quickly build and query a warehouse in Fabric. Copilot offers advice and best practices, autocomplete code, help fix and document code, and offer assistance with data prep, modeling, and analysis.

fabricroadmap.title: VARCHAR(MAX)/VARBINARY(MAX) types
fabricroadmap.summary: Users can define columns with VARCHAR(MAX)/VARBINARY(MAX) types in Data warehouse to store string or binary data up to 1 MB. In SQL endpoint for the Lakehouse, the string types in Delta tables are represented as VARCHAR(MAX) without truncation to 8 KB. The performance differences between the queries that are working with VARCHAR(MAX) and VARCHAR(8000) types are minimized, which enables users to use large types without significant performance penalty.

fabricroadmap.title: String performance improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: Operations on strings (VARCHAR(N)) are common in T-SQL queries. Performance improvements on string functions and operators that are working with strings boosts the performance of the queries that use LIKE predicates, [string functions](/sql/t-sql/functions/string-functions-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver16&preserve-view=true) and comparison operators in WHERE predicates, and operators like GROUP BY, ORDER BY, JOIN that are working with string types.

fabricroadmap.title: VARCHAR(MAX)/VARBINARY(MAX) types
fabricroadmap.summary: Users can define columns with VARCHAR(MAX)/VARBINARY(MAX) types in Data Warehouse to store string or binary data up to 16 MB.

fabricroadmap.title: MERGE (T-SQL)
fabricroadmap.summary: The MERGE T-SQL command for Fabric Data Warehouse brings the power of comparison logic and DML into a single step by allowing you to INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE a Target table based on matching conditions between your Source & Target table. Standardize your SQL transformations in one easy-to-read statement with MERGE.

fabricroadmap.title: Schema Compare in VS Code for Fabric Warehouse
fabricroadmap.summary: The Schema Compare feature in VS Code allows developers to compare database schemas between Fabric Warehouse projects or between a project and a live warehouse. Key capabilities include: Detecting differences: Quickly identify changes in tables, views, procedures, and other objects. Visual comparison: Provides an intuitive UI showing added, removed, or modified objects. Deployment support: Generate update scripts or DacFx packages to synchronize schemas safely. CI/CD integration: Helps maintain consistent schemas across environments by supporting version-controlled updates.

fabricroadmap.title: Full Query Text in Query Insights
fabricroadmap.summary: Full query text support in the Query Insights captures enables precise troubleshooting and analysis without the previous 8,000‑character truncation limit.

fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Warehouse offers Direct Connectivity as an opt-in connection mode. When enabled, your client connects directly to the Warehouse SQL front end using TDS redirect — reducing latency and significantly improving reliability for long-running and stateful connections such as large query executions, BI tool sessions, and application workloads that maintain persistent connections.

fabricroadmap.title: Data Grid Improvements in Data Warehouse & SQL Endpoint - Milestone 2
fabricroadmap.summary: The Data Grid feature for data warehouses and SQL analytics endpoints includes: Data Handling: Supports large datasets with virtualization for performance. fabricroadmap.title: Pre/Post Scripts in GIT & Deployment Workflows
fabricroadmap.summary: Allow users to define scripts that run automatically immediately before (pre-script) and immediately after (post-script) a warehouse deployment or git operations. This gives teams a controlled hook to prepare the environment beforehand and finalize or clean up afterward.

fabricroadmap.title: Reliable Warehouse Connectivity via TDS Redirect
fabricroadmap.summary: TDS Redirect introduces an opt-in connectivity mode for Fabric Data Warehouse that improves connection reliability by allowing supported SQL clients to establish a direct connection to the Warehouse after the initial handshake. By reducing intermediate proxy hops, this approach delivers more stable and resilient connections, particularly for long-running and stateful workloads such as ETL pipelines and reporting scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: DATE_BUCKET() - simplify analytics on datetime values
fabricroadmap.summary: The `DATE_BUCKET()` function groups dates into buckets of arbitrary length and returns the starting date of each bucket. OAP works in conjunction with other network security controls, such as Workspace Private Link, to provide comprehensive protection against data leaks and ensure compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.

fabricroadmap.summary: Query Insights will now present the amount of data scanned during query execution, spilt up by memory, disk and remote.

fabricroadmap.title: Warehouse Migration Assistant
fabricroadmap.summary: Designed to accelerate the migration of SQL Server, Synapse dedicated SQL pools, and other warehouses to the Fabric Data Warehouse, users will be able to migrate the code and data from the source database, automatically converting the source schema and code to Fabric Data Warehouse, helping with data migration, and providing AI powered assistance.

fabricroadmap.title: Scalar user-defined functions (UDFs)
fabricroadmap.summary: SQL native scalar user-defined functions (UDFs) facilitate the migration to Microsoft Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint by enabling custom procedural code reuse in T-SQL, with a focus on inlining scalar UDFs for enhanced performance and efficiency

fabricroadmap.title: Search, Filter, Sort in Object Explorer - Fabric Web Editor
fabricroadmap.summary: In the data warehouse, SQL developers use Object Explorer to navigate and manage database objects. They can also add existing data warehouses, SQL analytics endpoints from lake houses, and mirrored databases to query across databases. This feature aims to simplify sorting, searching, filtering, pinning, and collapsing database objects across databases in object explorer for easier management.

fabricroadmap.title: Data Clustering
fabricroadmap.summary: Data Clustering enables faster read performance by allowing users to specify columns for co-locating data on ingestion and perform file skipping on read.

fabricroadmap.title: Alter Table - Drop/sp_rename column
fabricroadmap.summary: Alter Table - Drop Column & sp_rename column will enable customers to alter their table definition by dropping and renaming columns. This is in addition to existing Alter Table functionality which supports adding new column and is in production today.

fabricroadmap.title: Temporary tables (session scoped)
fabricroadmap.summary: Session scoped, parquet backed temporary tables enable customers to store intermediate result sets for repeated access but are not required to persist permanently. They work as a regular, permament table but disappear when the connection is closed.

fabricroadmap.title: Identity columns
fabricroadmap.summary: Identity columns are numeric columns that automatically increment with each new row value that is inserted into a table with an Identity column defined.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for SQL analytics endpoint
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot for Data Warehouse is the ultimate paired programmer, and productivity booster for any skill level developer – from data professionals to analysts. It is designed to accelerate warehouse development by leveraging generative AI to simplify and automate Data Warehouse creation, analysis, and management. This feature enables Copilot usage in the SQL analytics endpoint.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for Data Warehouse: Sidecar Chat
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot for Data Warehouse is the ultimate paired programmer, and productivity booster for any skill level developer – from data professionals to analysts. It is designed to accelerate warehouse development by leveraging generative AI to simplify and automate Data Warehouse creation, analysis, and management.This feature introduces the Copilot sidecar chat pane. Use the chat pane to ask questions about your warehouse to Copilot through natural language. Use cases include: Natural Language to SQL: Ask Copilot a question about your warehouse data and receive a generated SQL query catered to your

fabricroadmap.title: COPY INTO - Support Workspace Identity
fabricroadmap.summary: COPY INTO - Support Workspace Identity – Support workspace-scoped identity as a credential option, allowing secure storage access and on-behalf-of enforcement without credential management.

fabricroadmap.title: Warehouse snapshots (Generally Available)
fabricroadmap.summary: This capability allows users to access a consistent read only version of data from a specific point in time, even if they attempt to access it during an ongoing ETL process. Fabric DW is committed to empowering businesses with reliable and consistent data, enabling them to make informed decisions with confidence.As read-only child items of the parent warehouse, warehouse snapshots offer a consistent and stable view of your data, ensuring that analytical workloads remain unaffected by ongoing changes or ETL operations.

fabricroadmap.title: Custom SQL Pools
fabricroadmap.summary: Custom SQL Pools will provide user managed workload isolation boundaries as well as the ability to control the burstable capacity limit.

fabricroadmap.title: Managing Multi-Warehouse Dependencies with DacFx
fabricroadmap.summary: DacFx support for cross-warehouse references allows developers to define and manage dependencies between objects in different Fabric Warehouses. For example, a table in Warehouse A might reference a view in Warehouse B. With DacFx: These references can be tracked and versioned in Git, just like regular schema changes. Deployments can validate and update cross-warehouse objects safely, reducing the risk of broken references. It supports incremental, non-destructive deployments, ensuring that changes in one warehouse don’t unexpectedly break dependencies in another.Cyclic dependencies between wa

fabricroadmap.title: Migration Assistant - Direct connect to the source system
fabricroadmap.summary: The live connectivity in Migration Assistant for Fabric Data Warehouse enables customers to connect directly to their source systems and migrate metadata without generating or uploading a DACPAC. The new approach simplifies and accelerates the early stages of migration while reducing manual preparation and risk. Customers continue to benefit from the familiar, guided Migration Assistant experience as they modernize their data warehouses to Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: Migrate to Fabric DW using SQL files
fabricroadmap.summary: Migrate to Fabric Data Warehouse enables customers to upload a compressed (zip) of .sql files to initiate the migration. The new approach simplifies and accelerates the early stages of migration while reducing manual preparation and risk. Customers continue to benefit from the familiar, guided Migration Assistant experience as they modernize their data warehouses to Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: ALTER TABLE support inside transactions (Generally Available)
fabricroadmap.summary: Treating schema changes as transactional aligns with atomicity and isolation guarantees. If any part of the transaction fails, everything is rolled back, preserving data integrity. This capability is especially useful for automated pipelines and CI/CD workflows, where schema changes must be applied safely and predictably.With this release, Fabric Data Warehouse supports executing the following inside an explicit transaction:ALTER TABLE Add nullable columnsALTER TABLE Drop columnsALTER TABLE Add or drop NOT ENFORCED PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, and FOREIGN KEY constraintsExecute multiple ALTER TABLE st

fabricroadmap.title: ALTER COLUMN (Public Preview)
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables users to modify the definition of an existing column in a Fabric DW table, specifically allowing changes to the column’s data type and size.https://community.fabric.microsoft.com/t5/Fabric-Updates-Blogs/Simplify-Schema-Changes-in-Fabric-Data-Warehouse-with-ALTER/ba-p/5177593

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Web: Streamlined Git and Deployment Pipeline Support with DacFx
fabricroadmap.summary: DacFx onboarding in the Fabric Web editor enables seamless Git integration and supports deployment pipelines for Fabric Warehouse. With DacFx, developers can reliably manage schema changes, version control database projects, and execute incremental, non-destructive deployments directly from the web editor. This integration ensures that changes are tracked, deployments are safe, and pipelines can be automated, aligning with best practices for CI/CD in enterprise data environments.

fabricroadmap.title: SSMS 22.3 Support for Fabric Warehouse
fabricroadmap.summary: SSMS 22.3 provides key capabilities for Fabric Warehouse, including: Browse and Connectivity: Explore and connect to Fabric Warehouses directly from SSMS. Warehouse Actions: Ability to extract the definition of a warehouse from SSMS using Export Data tier application.

fabricroadmap.title: Workspace-Friendly Connections
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric workspace connection strings often contain complex, encoded server names that make it difficult for developers to identify or manage connections easily.With Friendly workspace server name, developers can configure a friendly server name for a workspace that helps connections simpler to manage.

fabricroadmap.title: MERGE (T-SQL)
fabricroadmap.summary: The MERGE T-SQL command for Fabric Data Warehouse brings the power of comparison logic and DML into a single step by allowing you to INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE a Target table based on matching conditions between your Source & Target table. Standardize your SQL transformations in one easy-to-read statement with MERGE.

fabricroadmap.title: BULK INSERT
fabricroadmap.summary: The BULK INSERT statement is used to ingest files in Fabric DW (similar to COPY INTO). with the BULK INERT function we are enabling migration from SQL Server to Fabric DW with minimal code changes. The customers would need to rewrite their code and external tools that use BULK INSERT to migrate to COPY INTO as a prerequisite for migrating to Fabric DW.In addition, BULK INSERT support some traditional on-prem options that are not available in COPY INTO.

fabricroadmap.title: BCP
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Data Warehouse will support the bcp utility and the TDS Bulk Load API, enabling high-performance data ingestion from a variety of client tools such as bcp, SSIS, and Azure Data Factory. This integration simplifies bulk data loading into Fabric DW and supports scalable, efficient workflows. Centralized support for these APIs ensures consistency across ingestion pipelines and improves interoperability with existing tools.<br/>An example of a bcp command that loads file content into a DW table:<br/>```bcp dbo.artists in gold_artist.txt -d TextDW -c -S myworkspace.datawarehouse.

fabricroadmap.title: JSON support
fabricroadmap.summary: JSON support in Fabric Datawarehouse enables processing of textual data formatted as JSON text. The new JSON features in Fabric DW are: FOR JSON query option that formats the query results as JSON text. This was one of the features that is requested on Microsoft Fabric Idea site. JSON scalar functions that can also be used in Azure SQL database. In addition to the existing JSON scalar functions (ISJSON, JSON\_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, and JSON\_MODIFY), Fabric DW is suporting the latest JSON functions that exist in Azure SQL Database – JSON\_PATH\_EXISTS, JSON\_OBJECT, and JSON\_ARRAY.

fabricroadmap.title: SQL audit logs
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature tracks database events and writes them to an audit log, thereby allowing customers to query the audit file using sys.fn_get_audit_file_v2 for auditing and compliance.

fabricroadmap.title: AI Functions in DW
fabricroadmap.summary: AI functions natively available in T-SQL allow you to seamlessly integrate powerful language capabilities into your queries. You can analyze sentiment, classify text into predefined labels, extract contextual insights, translate between languages, correct grammar, or run flexible, prompt-based instructions—all directly from T-SQL. This feature enables intelligent data processing and enrichment without leaving the database environment.For example:<br/>```SELECT ai_analyze_sentiment(text), ai_classify(text, 'hardware', 'software') FROM reviews```

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Functions in DW
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric function support in T-SQL enables users to call external data functions directly from their SQL queries within the Data Warehouse. This allows for advanced processing, enrichment, and transformation while centralizing logic and promoting code reuse across different engines and workloads. By embedding Fabric functions into SQL, teams can streamline operations and maintain consistency across platforms.For example, if you defined a `my_fabric_function` user data function, you cna call it from T-SQL code using the folowing T-SQL syntax:<br/>```SELECT , my_fabric_function(param1, param

fabricroadmap.title: Collate Clause Support in Warehouse
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables users to specify collations on individual columns, rather than relying solely on the artifact-level collation. Users will be able to use the ‘COLLATE’ command with the CREATE Table / ALTER Table ADD Nullable colum / SELECT INTO / CTAS statements to define the collation for their VARCHAR / CHAR fields. This release also includes support for the 'DATABASE_DEFAULT' collation. All Fabric warehouses by default are configured with case-sensitive (CS) collation Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8. You can also create warehouses with case-insensitive (CI) collation - Latin1_General_100_C

fabricroadmap.title: Optimized DELETE
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature will improve the performance of DELETE data from Fabric Data Warehouse tables.

fabricroadmap.title: Reliable Fabric Warehouse Connectivity using Redirect Mode for general workspaces
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Warehouse Connectivity Redirect Mode optimizes connection paths by bypassing unnecessary network hops and routing traffic directly to the Data Warehouse. This improves connection reliability during deployments and reduces disruption from infrastructure changes, while delivering better performance and consistency for large‑dataset and long running workloads.

fabricroadmap.title: Scalar User-defined functions (UDFs) - Procedural SQL
fabricroadmap.summary: SQL native, computation-based scalar UDFs now support WHILE loops, multiple RETURN statements and deeply nested IF-THEN-ELSE blocks in the function body. They can also be used in queries that include Common Table Expressions (CTEs), and within GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY clauses.

fabricroadmap.title: Job events in workspace monitoring
fabricroadmap.summary: Job events are being added to workspace monitoring. Job events allow you to monitor job status (e.g., refreshing a semantic model, running a scheduled pipeline, or running a notebook) and analyze job performance over time.

fabricroadmap.title: Organize multitasking tabs in groups
fabricroadmap.summary: Stay focused when working across many open items by grouping tabs. Create named groups, organize related work, and collapse or expand them as needed.

fabricroadmap.title: Pin and unpin multitasking tabs
fabricroadmap.summary: Allow users to pin/unpin tabs.

fabricroadmap.title: Open the multitasking tab in new browser tab
fabricroadmap.summary: Allow users toright click on a multitasking tab and open it in a new browser tab, similar to the web browser experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Allow users to reorder open workspaces in the nav bar
fabricroadmap.summary: Currently, users can open multiple workspaces simultaneously and switch between them via the navigation bar. However, the order of these workspace icons is fixed based on the sequence in which they were opened.This creates friction for users who frequently multitask across workspaces and want to organize their open items in a way that better reflects their workflow priorities.This feature allows users to reorder open workspace icons in the navigation bar through drag-and-drop interaction, enabling greater control and efficiency in multitasking.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Remote MCP (Public Preview)
fabricroadmap.summary: We’re launching the public preview of Fabric Remote MCP — a secure, cloud-hosted execution engine that lets AI agents and automation tools perform authenticated actions in Fabric using a standardized protocol. This eliminates the need for custom integrations and enables seamless automation of tasks like workspace provisioning and item deployment. It’s a major step toward an AI-native Fabric experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Support object explorer to reduce context switching in item and workspace navigation
fabricroadmap.summary: Introduce an Object Explorer panel to improve navigation efficiency across items in the open workspace. It will provide a structured, hierarchical view of related objects—supporting quick access to child items and easy traversal to parent items. This enables a more intuitive experience, especially in complex solutions, and brings Fabric closer to the familiar navigation patterns found in IDEs.

fabricroadmap.title: CI/CD - GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency support
fabricroadmap.summary: Ability to connect Fabric workspace to repositories which reside on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Core REST API generally available
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Core REST APIs are now generally available. This marks a significant milestone in the evolution of Microsoft Fabric, a platform that has been meticulously designed to empower developers and businesses alike with a comprehensive suite of tools and services.The Core REST APIs are the backbone of Microsoft Fabric, providing the essential building blocks for a myriad of functionalities within the platform. They are designed to improve efficiency, reduce manual effort, increase accuracy, and lead to faster processing times. These APIs help scale operations more easily and efficiently as the

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Core REST APIs support Service Principal
fabricroadmap.summary: Enablement of Service Principal support in Microsoft Fabric REST API is a pivotal enhancement for the automation of customers deployment and management of environments.The ability to manage principal permissions for Fabric workspaces, as well as the creation and management of Fabric artifacts like eventhouse and lakehouse, is crucial for the automation of provisioning workflows. By end of July 2024, Service Principal will already be supported by few automation scenarios, such as Fabric Workspace management, Power BI Report management, Power BI Semantic Models management and Fabric Capacity.

fabricroadmap.title: Parent-child items in workspaces
fabricroadmap.summary: Some Fabric items have children items such as Lakehouse, Data Warehouse, etc. This feature enables you to easily view the parent-child items relationship in workspace UI and also makes the items list cleaner.

fabricroadmap.title: Persistent filters in workspaces
fabricroadmap.summary: Currently, the workspace filters aren't persistent. You must reapply filters each time upon returning to the workspace. We heard your feedback and plan to enable persistent filters for improved navigation.

fabricroadmap.title: Customizable left navigation bar
fabricroadmap.summary: We learned from you that the frequently used capabilities vary for everyone based on their roles and job to be done during a certain period time. To better improve productivity, we plan to make the left navigation bar customizable. You can pin or unpin an entry point on the left navigation bar according to your own preferences.

fabricroadmap.title: REST API - Export and import multiple items in a single call
fabricroadmap.summary: Today, when Importing multiple item definitions, it required multiple API calls, but that requires very deep understanding of how Fabric works in order to make it a successful deployment:- Developer needs to know the order of deployment, based on how items are related to each other.- Developer needs to update the relations of each item, by familiarizing itself with its definition, and swapping the GUIDs of the dependent items.This requires a lot of coding and technical deep dive by developers and its hard to scale. That's why we are building the option to Import multiple items in a single API

fabricroadmap.title: Service Principal support for Azure DevOps
fabricroadmap.summary: For a complete automation story for CI/CD and Git APIs, we will support working with Service principal when running the [Fabric Git APIs](/rest/api/fabric/core/git).This will allow devs to call these APIs with an App created in Entra, and has access to the workspace.Additoinal info: As we are adding also support for cross-tenant Authentication for Azure DevOps, the SPN used to call Fabric APIs won't automatically be the same identity used to work against Azure Repos. If the same SPN is to be used to access the repo, make sure the SPN has access. You would also need to setup the App ID and Secr

fabricroadmap.title: Git integration - Cross-tenant Authentication to Azure DevOps
fabricroadmap.summary: Today, users of Fabric can work against Azure DevOps only using the same user they are logged into Fabric with.With this feature, we will enable (in addition to current single-sign-on experience) to connect using a separate user, that can be from a different tenant as well.This can enable few scenarios for different organizations: When the org uses a different tenant for Azure DevOps than the tenant used in Fabric. When the org uses Fabric with multiple tenants (such as dev/test/prod workspaces). In cases of guest user in a tenant (B2B).

fabricroadmap.title: Git integration - compare code changes
fabricroadmap.summary: When developers want to sync their workspace with the git repo, they want to view the changes made before taking actions.With this feature we will enable viewing the exact changes since the last sync between the workspace and the branch, as well as where those changes are.It will be shown as code compare experience that is familiar to developers. Devs can see what items and files have been changed, see the exact code changes and whether it is in a Fabric workspace, or in the repo.

fabricroadmap.title: Deployment pipelines new UI
fabricroadmap.summary: As Deployment pipelines evolve into a platform tool (fabric’s), it necessitates modifications in its current design to accommodate Fabric from various angles such as UX alignments, scalability, and advanced features, among others. The new UI of Deployment pipelines introduce a fresh user interface for the creation process and the pipeline’s main page, along with some UX improvements. There’s also a shift in the deployment operation where instead of deploying to the next stage, you’re now deploying to your current stage. Other than that, all functionalities have stayed the same so anything you

fabricroadmap.title: Extension Workloads - Onelake Shortcut support
fabricroadmap.summary: We are enabeling Shortcut Support From and To Items that have been developed over the Workload Development Kit. This will allow partners and cusotmers to provide richer and more integrated experiences for their items.

fabricroadmap.title: Extension Workloads - Storing Item state within Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allowes workloads to store the Item State within Fabric, providing them with a way to build Workloads that don't need to store any user data outside of the customers tenant.

fabricroadmap.title: Extension Workloads - CRUD support over public APIs
fabricroadmap.summary: Allowing Items from Extension workloads to be managed over the stanard public Fabric APIs

fabricroadmap.title: Improve '+New' experience in workspace: Item grouped by JTBD
fabricroadmap.summary: Current the +New dropdown in workspace is a long and flat list. We kept getting feedback from customers that they expect items to be grouped by JTBD so that they can easily find them. We also add the capability to let user favourite the item types for quick create.

fabricroadmap.title: Workspace filters/search support nested folders
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature provides user capability to filer/search by keyword in entire workspace or entire folder including all its children.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric navigation experience improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: Currently, users access various workloads—such as Power BI, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, and Data Science—through the button in the lower-left corner. While this approach was intended to provide flexibility, we’ve heard that it can be confusing, leaving users uncertain about when and why to switch between workloads.Now, we’re refining how users open and interact with the product to simplify the workflow and make navigation more intuitive.

fabricroadmap.title: Enable users to adjust list column width in workload home, browse and workspace view
fabricroadmap.summary: Currently the columns in Fabric workload home, browse and workspace page cannot be expanded to display full object name. The maximum width allowed for the name column is determined by the screen width. This feature improves the column width resizing experience and allow users to set up unlimited column width. And at same time, ensure a non-broken experience of the table and other columns.

fabricroadmap.title: Add job capacity information in Monitor Hub
fabricroadmap.summary: We’re introducing a new “Capacity” column for all item types in the Monitor Hub to help users gain a clearer understanding of how capacity is being utilized. When you experience a “capacity throttle” in the future, you’ll be able to refer to the Monitor Hub for insights and clues that may help in diagnosing the issue.

fabricroadmap.title: Recommended task flow for Power BI workspaces
fabricroadmap.summary: With a single click, you can create the recommended task flows for your Power BI workspaces, which only contain Power BI items in it. Creating task flow automatically assigns each item in your workspace to the relevant tasks. This allows you to view the relationships between tasks, filter the list of item types, and more easily locate, organize, and manage the items you created.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric workload developer kit
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature now extends to additional workloads and offers a robust developer toolkit for designing, developing, and interoperating with Microsoft Fabric using frontend SDKs and backend REST APIs. Introducing the Microsoft Fabric Workload Development Kit. The Microsoft Fabric platform now provides a mechanism for ISVs and developers to integrate their new and existing applications natively into Fabric’s workload hub. This integration provides the ability to add net new capabilities to Fabric in a consistent experience without leaving their Fabric workspace, thereby accelerating data driven ou

fabricroadmap.title: Power BI Embedded over Direct Lake
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI Embedded over Direct Lake mode semantic models is enabled, including full automation based on Fabric REST APIs. This allows ISVs to deploy and manage a solution, based on Direct Lake semantic models, to a very large number of their customer tenants. Direct Lake mode is a groundbreaking new engine capability to analyze very large datasets in Power BI. The technology is based on the idea of loading parquet-formatted files directly from a data lake, without having to query a Warehouse or SQL analytics endpoint, and without having to import or duplicate data into a Power BI semantic model

fabricroadmap.title: Deployment pipelines new UI
fabricroadmap.summary: As Deployment pipelines evolve into a platform tool (fabric’s), it necessitates modifications in its current design to accommodate Fabric from various angles such as UX alignments, scalability, and advanced features, among others. The new UI of Deployment pipelines introduce a fresh user interface for the creation process and the pipeline’s main page, along with some UX improvements. There’s also a shift in the deployment operation where instead of deploying to the next stage, you’re now deploying to your current stage. Other than that, all functionalities have stayed the same so anything you

fabricroadmap.title: Deployment pipelines Fabric APIs Phase II
fabricroadmap.summary: In line with Fabric alignment, we are finalizing the public APIs for the Deployment pipelines on the Fabric platform, following the initial batch of APIs released in May 2024. While the May release provided the ability to retrieve existing deployment pipeline details and stages, the upcoming release will introduce APIs for their modification, workspace addition/removal, access control, and administrative tasks. The complete list is provided below.Service Principal support for Deployment pipelines APIsAdd Deployment Pipeline Role AssignmentDelete Deployment Pipeline Role AssignmentGet Deploymen

fabricroadmap.title: Git integration folders support
fabricroadmap.summary: Folder support with Git integration will empower users to uphold their folder structure consistently across both the Fabric workspace and the connected Git repository. Modifications to workspace folders containing Fabric items will be accurately mirrored in both platofrms, facilitating seamless synchronization between Git and Fabric, even when handling intricate folder hierarchies.

fabricroadmap.title: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise support
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Git integration is broadening its compatibility by adding support for GitHub as a provider. Given GitHub's widespread adoption as a leading source control tool, this expansion will grant organizations relying on GitHub the opportunity to harness Fabric Git integration, ensuring synchronization between their fabric workspaces and Git repositories. GitHub will come in the addition to the existing Azure DevOps support, offering all of the same familiar tools and capabilities. Developers will have the ability to connect to GiHub using their personal access tokens, ensuring a precise connect

fabricroadmap.title: Git integration - enhanced branching capabilities
fabricroadmap.summary: This update to Fabric Git integration introduces enhanced branch-related capabilities, providing users with a seamless method to work in isolation, an essential aspect of any workflow. This release encompasses several improvements to the connection between Fabric and Git branches: Branching Out to New Workspace: Users can effortlessly branch out to new work environments with just a few clicks. This feature facilitates the creation of a new workspace synced with a corresponding new branch, ready for developers to begin their work. Once tasks are completed, merging back can easily be done via th

fabricroadmap.title: Instant and summarized help answers in the Fabric Help Pane
fabricroadmap.summary: A search experience that considers the user intent (search keywords) to propose ML powered instant answers and self-help resources in the help pane

fabricroadmap.title: .NET SDK for Fabric REST APIs
fabricroadmap.summary: The Fabric REST API provides developers with programmatic access to manage and interact with Microsoft Fabric resources. It enables developers to automate a wide array of tasks, including data integration, data warehousing, big data analytics, deployment process automation, new tenant provisioning, and more.The .NET SDK is a wrapper library that simplifies the communication with the Fabric REST API and handles the authentication, serialization, and error handling for you.The .NET SDK for Fabric REST API exposes the following endpoints:1. Capacities: List capacities2. Workspaces: Create, update

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Terraform Provider
fabricroadmap.summary: Utilizing the Terraform Provider for Fabric enables users to automate and streamline deployment and management processes in a declarative manner. This ensures that deployments and management tasks are executed accurately and consistently, thereby reducing manual errors.Fabric Terraform Provider will help you with: Keep track of all changes in source version control solutions, like Azure DevOps, GitHub. Enable DevOps processes by implementing testing and validation strategies before deploying to production. Enhance scalability and flexibility for deployments. Boost the speed and reliability of

fabricroadmap.title: Improved discoverability of the Help Pane in the product
fabricroadmap.summary: Through user feedback, we heard that users do not know where to get help in product. Through this feature, all Fabric users will be able to navigate to to the help pane from error messages, support page, and the global search boxto get contextual help.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Extensibility Toolkit - Variable support
fabricroadmap.summary: Items built with the Fabric Extensibility Toolkit can now pick up and resolve Variables, allowing them to dynamically adapt to the context in which they run. When a user opens an Item, the Item automatically evaluates any referenced Variables—such as workspace metadata, user‑provided parameters, or environment‑specific values—and replaces them with their resolved results. This enables Items to behave consistently across different workspaces and scenarios, while still responding to variable-driven configuration.

fabricroadmap.title: Item Soft-Delete and Recovery -  Workspace recycle bin in UI
fabricroadmap.summary: Item soft-delete and recovery offer a secure and efficient way to manage deleted items. When an item is deleted, it is moved to workspace recycle bin and retained for a defined retention period. During this retention period, users can restore items or permanently remove them through UI.

fabricroadmap.title: Variable Library - Item reference variable type
fabricroadmap.summary: Offerring a new variable type in Variable library item, which keeps item ID and its workspace ID, and enforce role permissions and better experience. Is supported in Shortcut for lakehouse, Data pipeline, UDF and and Notebook's in-code.

fabricroadmap.title: Variable Library - Connection reference variable type
fabricroadmap.summary: A new variable type is added to Variable library item, which keeps Cloud connection ID, enforce permissions and brings better experience for parameterize connections in CI/CD as allowing customize connection based on deployment stage.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Extensibility Toolkit - Workload validation Improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: The Fabric Extensibility Toolkit (FET) introduces Validation Improvements to streamline readiness checks for Public Preview and GA stages. A new self-verification tool empowers developers to validate workloads independently, ensuring compliance with Fabric standards before submission. In addition, we’ve enhanced documentation for validation workflows and upgraded the partner validation reports, providing clearer insights, actionable feedback, and alignment with certification requirements. These improvements reduce friction, accelerate approval timelines, and give partners greater confidence in

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Python SDK GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Python SDK GA alllows to build, automate, and integrate with Microsoft Fabric faster.With GA stability and support, developers and ISVs can programmatically manage Fabric items, workspaces, and operations using clean, idiomatic Python APIs—designed for production-scale automation, CI/CD, and embedded experiences.

fabricroadmap.title: Associate an identity with Fabric items and schedules
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric items and their schedules today implicitly execute under user identities (owner or creator), which makes production workloads fragile: pipelines, schedules, copy jobs, and shortcuts break when owners leave the organization or their tokens expire, and existing takeover flows only shift the dependency to another user rather than removing it. With this release, Fabric introduces associated Identity: a durable, user-selected execution identity that can be attached to an item through new UI and APIs, starting with Workspace Identity support and Schedule Run-as. You will be able to

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Monitor and Fabric Data Integration
fabricroadmap.summary: You can now cross correlate business data with observability data as Azure Monitor log is available in Microsoft Fabric through OneLake Shortcuts — without duplicating or moving data. Customers can analyze Azure Monitor logs alongside business, operational, and analytics data already stored in Fabric. This allows teams to correlate observability insights with enterprise data in a single analytics environment, reduce data movement and storage overhead, and unlock richer cross-domain scenarios such as operational analytics, cost optimization, security investigations, and business-impact analysis

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration provider - GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency support
fabricroadmap.summary: Ability to connect Fabric workspace to repositories which reside on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency

fabricroadmap.title: Enable developers to focus on one key editor pane and hide sidebar
fabricroadmap.summary: When focusing on editing an Item developers need an option to maximize the available window space for the editor pane. This is a core need when working on Item editing, but it also addresses the crowding that can occur in the UI due to multiple levels of navigation and side panels between the shell and various extensions.This feature allows users to hide their navigation side bar so that they can be more focused on the main page.

fabricroadmap.title: Hotkey support for quick navigation
fabricroadmap.summary: Enable hotkey functionality to support efficient management of open items. By reducing reliance on mouse interactions, it streamlines multitasking workflows, enhances productivity, and minimizes context-switching, making it easier for users to stay focused and manage complex tasks simultaneously.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - Selective Branching

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph delivers reliable performance at billion scale
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph is designed to operate at very large scale, supporting graphs with billions of elements while maintaining predictable performance and reliability. Ongoing investments improve query stability, ingestion throughput, and service resiliency. Operational visibility is enhanced by exposing detailed ingestion failure information and clearer diagnostic signals, enabling customers to identify, understand, and resolve issues more quickly as graph workloads scale into production.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph enables fast insight with no/low code graph modelling, querying and exploration
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph provides low code and no code experiences for modelling graphs, building queries, and exploring results. Customers can define graph models, manage reusable queries, and inspect outputs through UI driven workflows without requiring deep GQL expertise. These experiences lower the barrier to entry for analysts and application builders, while still allowing advanced users to drop down to full GQL for complex scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph makes connected data accessible through natural language data agents
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph integrates with Fabric Data Agent and supports NL2GQL, enabling users to ask questions about graph data in natural language. Queries are translated into GQL, executed against the graph, and returned as grounded results. Users can inspect the executed query or navigate back to the graph experience for deeper exploration. This capability allows Fabric Graph to participate directly in agent driven and Copilot scenarios while maintaining transparency and trust.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph expands GQL support for real world relationship queries
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph increases GQL feature coverage to support richer relationship modeling and investigation scenarios. This includes dynamic nested data, OPTIONAL MATCH, extended FOR semantics (IS SOURCE OF, IS DESTINATION OF, COLLECT ONE), result shaping functions (NODES, EDGES, INNER NODES), quantified simple edge patterns, and shortest path queries.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph enforces OneLake security for governed graph access
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph conforms to OneLake security so that access controls defined over lake data are enforced consistently when data is represented and queried as a graph. Row , column , and object level policies apply end to end, preventing graphs from becoming an alternate access path. This alignment ensures customers can adopt Fabric Graph without introducing new security models or weakening existing governance and compliance controls.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph supports private network access for enterprise environments
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph supports private connectivity using Fabric private endpoints and private links. This allows customers to access graph workloads over private networks, keep traffic off the public internet, and deploy Fabric Graph in locked down enterprise network environments. The service validates graph APIs under private access configurations and propagates the required access context for trusted service to service communication.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for Fabric Graph
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph complies with Fabric Workspace Outbound Access Protection (OAP). When OAP is enabled, graph workloads enforce outbound network policies, allowing connections only to approved destinations such as managed private endpoints. Non compliant outbound calls are blocked and surfaced clearly. This ensures Fabric Graph aligns with enterprise network security requirements and helps prevent unintended or unauthorized data exfiltration.

fabricroadmap.title: Ontology Health
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing Ontology Health in Microsoft Fabric to help modelers quickly assess whether an ontology is ready for real-world use. With this capability, ontology quality is continuously evaluated across three core areas—foundation, validation, and refinement—ensuring models are structurally sound, properly configured, and operationally ready. With this capability, you can: Identify structural issues and inconsistencies through foundation checks to ensure the ontology is sound. Verify required configurations using validation checks to confirm completeness and correctness. Improve clarity,

fabricroadmap.title: Rules for Ontology
fabricroadmap.summary: The rules feature of ontology (preview) lets you automate and manage event-driven alerts directly within your entity types. With the integrated capabilities of Fabric Activator, you can achieve real-time monitoring and response for your business entities. This feature allows you to define alerts that monitor properties across every instance of an entity type, to ensure comprehensive, ongoing oversight.Rules transform ontologies from static information models to dynamic and operational model. Now you are capable of automatically initiating business processes through alerts and automated actions

fabricroadmap.title: Resource Links - Link PBI Reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Resource Links let you attach resources to the entity types they describe, so insights live alongside the data model that powers them. Starting with Power BI reports, when someone explores an entity in your ontology, they can immediately see the relevant Power BI reports that show how that data is analyzed, monitored, and used without needing to search across tools or guess which report applies.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Operations Agent
fabricroadmap.summary: We are delivering Outbound Access Protection for Operations Agent in Microsoft Fabric, enabling administrators to enforce workspace-level security controls on all outbound actions performed by AI-driven automation.With this capability, you canEnsure all outbound actions such as triggering Power Automate flows, executing Fabric jobs, or sending Teams notifications are governed by administrator-defined connection rules.Block outbound connections by default when OAP is enabled, permitting traffic only through approved endpoints to prevent unauthorized data movement.Leverage a hybrid enforcement m

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Foundry IQ] - Ontology integration with Foundry IQ
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates with Azure AI Foundry to provide data scientists and AI builders with rich semantic context for training, grounding, and fine-tuning models and agents. By connecting ontology-defined business concepts, entity relationships, and domain vocabulary to your AI workflows, Foundry IQ enables more reliable agent behavior, improved reasoning over business processes, and better alignment between AI outputs and the real-world structure of your enterprise.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for A365] - Ontology integration with Agent 365
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates natively with Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent 365, providing AI agents with a rich semantic source of truth for reasoning over your business data. When users ask questions in natural language, agents leverage the ontology to understand the relationships between business entities, interpret intent consistently, and deliver grounded, accurate answers drawn directly from your enterprise data — all within the familiar Microsoft 365 experience.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Data Agent] - Ontology integration with Data Agent
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology empowers the Data Agent to query and reason over your business data using natural language, grounded in a well-defined semantic model. Users can ask complex analytical questions and receive trustworthy, explainable answers with citations that trace back to the underlying ontology and data sources — giving teams confidence that insights are accurate, verifiable, and rooted in the true structure of their enterprise data.

fabricroadmap.title: Modeling Untyped Properties
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allows users to create property definitions without immediately selecting a data type or binding to a data source. Users can define high‑level business concepts first and assign data types later when real data is bound, at which point the entity type updates automatically. This flexibility lets users model concepts early without needing to know data types or source details upfront.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology MCP Endpoint] Query Tools
fabricroadmap.summary: The Ontology MCP Endpoint provides a programmatic query surface that enables any AI agent or application to discover, explore, and reason over ontology data. Query tools support natural language search over ontology data, schema discovery through entity type and property listing, and structured entity/relationship traversal — giving developers and agents a single, consistent API to ask questions, retrieve answers, and build intelligent experiences grounded in your enterprise semantic layer.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Operational Agent] - Ontology integration with Operations Agent
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology enables operational agents to reason over your live business environment using natural language, providing frontline teams with explainable, trustworthy answers backed by citations. Operational agents use the ontology as their semantic backbone to interpret questions about asset status, process state, and operational relationships — delivering grounded insights that help operators make faster, better-informed decisions without needing to navigate multiple data systems.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security GA
fabricroadmap.summary: General availability of OneLake security's core features: folder, table, row, and column level security across all Fabric workloads.

fabricroadmap.title: Inbound network protection to OneLake with resource instance rules
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature offers a simple and secure way to restrict OneLake access to only your application's Azure resources, while blocking all other public access. It works by configuring resource instance rules specific to your designated Azure resource.

fabricroadmap.title: Smart caching for Amazon S3 shortcuts
fabricroadmap.summary: Smart caching for Amazon S3 shortcuts reduces egress costs and enhances performance by bringing data closer to the compute engine. Smart caching will egress data from S3 once, cache it locally in OneLake for a certain period. This way it eliminates the need for repeated data retrieval from S3. The cached data can be reused across multiple users, analytical engines, and scenarios that optimize the value a single egress.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcuts API
fabricroadmap.summary: A public REST API to automate creation and management of shortcut scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcuts Google cloud storage
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake will expand shortcut support to Google Cloud Storage, allowing virtualization of data without moving or duplicating it. This enables the integration of Google Cloud Storage data with Microsoft services like ADLS gen2, OneLake, Dataverse, and Amazon S3. The data will appear and work as if it was in OneLake and gives you a simple data lake that can span clouds.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - ReadWrite permission
fabricroadmap.summary: Configure write permissions for folders in a lakehouse using OneLake security. With this feature, viewers can be given selective write access to certain folders in the lakehouse enabling teams to write data without having Contributor or higher roles in the workspace.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - gated public preview
fabricroadmap.summary: Now with OneLake security, you can define access permissions once, and Fabric will enforce it consistently across all engines. Data owners can create security roles, refine permissions, and control access at the row and column levels to securely share data. For example, you can grant access to only certain folders, tables, or even rows in a lakehouse—restricting Personally Identifiable Information (PII) while keeping other data available. This security propagates automatically, so whether you query the data in SQL or visualize it in a Power BI report, you can only see what has been authorized.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - public preview (no sign-up)
fabricroadmap.summary: Now available for use without signing up, OneLake security allows you to set security once and have it enforced across all engines in Microsoft Fabric. Use granular permissions such as table, column, or row level security to limit access to sensitive data.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake shortcuts to on-premises data
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft OneLake shortcuts is expanding to include on-premises and network-restricted data sources. With this capability, you can unify your on-prem and cloud data in OneLake.During creation of shortcuts to AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or S3 compatible buckets, you will be able to optionally select an on-premises data gateway (OPDG) to establish connectivity.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake table shortcuts to Iceberg data
fabricroadmap.summary: With Microsoft OneLake, you can create table shortcuts to Iceberg data in other locations, and this data will appear automatically with the Delta Lake format.OneLake automatically produces virtualized Delta Lake metadata and makes it available through the OneLake shortcut. This means you can use your Iceberg data with all Fabric workloads that work with Delta Lake formatted data.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake malware scanning
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake malware protection helps secure your data by automatically scanning files for malicious content when they’re uploaded. It surfaces alerts and scan results for further action, providing built‑in protection for enterprise data without requiring additional infrastructure.

fabricroadmap.title: Databricks Unity Catalog support for OneLake
fabricroadmap.summary: Azure Databricks Unity Catalog Integration with Microsoft FabricYou will be able to access Azure Databricks Unity Catalog tables directly in Microsoft Fabric, making it even easier to unify Azure Databricks with Microsoft Fabric. From the Fabric portal, you can create and configure a new Azure Databricks Unity Catalog item in Fabric with just a few clicks. You can add a full catalog, a schema, or even individual tables to link and the management of this Azure Databricks item in OneLake—a shortcut connected to Unity Catalog—is automatically taken care of for you. This data acts like any other d

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake catalog - tables data preview and quick actions
fabricroadmap.summary: With this new feature, OneLake catalog can display user-defined descriptions for tables and columns, helping users quickly understand data context. Once a table is identified as relevant, users can instantly preview its data with a single click - streamlining discovery and accelerating informed decision-making. This enhancement fosters trust, promotes collaboration, and encourages a culture of data reuse across the organization.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Schema Definition, Preview and Drift
fabricroadmap.summary: Handling additional columns, reordered columns, missing columns, and duplicate rows remains one of the top challenges for users in the current Shortcut Transformations experience. This feature aims to allow users to define and preview schemas, rename columns, change data types, and handle various schema evolution scenarios applicable to file-based data transformation. With these capabilities, users can simplify complex schema management in file data processing and gain complete control using Shortcut Transformations. Define and preview your schema, rename columns, adjust data types, and seamle

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Excel to Delta
fabricroadmap.summary: You will soon be able to bring your Excel data directly into Fabric Lakehouse Delta tables without extra steps. This feature allows you to select multiple tabs from a single Excel workbook and load them into structured Delta tables. You can preview and align schemas, automatically handle column mapping, and ensure data types remain consistent. The ingestion process is optimized for speed and reliability. With this update, you can transition from familiar Excel workflows to modern lakehouse architecture effortlessly, making analytics faster and collaboration easier.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Customize ingestion with user configurations
fabricroadmap.summary: With the upcoming enhancements to Shortcut Transformations, you’ll be able to fully customize how you bring in data from CSV, Parquet, JSON, and Excel files. You can set file encoding, choose custom quote or escape characters for your data in case of CSV files. For CSV, Parquet and JSON files, you’ll have options to decide refresh mode (Append Only or Mirror) and schema mode (Dynamic or Fixed). All these controls will be available directly in the user interface, giving you more flexibility, reliability, and efficiency in managing your data ingestion and transformation workflows.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Enhanced monitoring experience
fabricroadmap.summary: With the latest improvements to Shortcut Transformations, you’ll have a much more transparent and actionable monitoring experience. You’ll be able to see detailed stats in the UI, including the number of rows read and written, files processed, and files skipped. Troubleshooting is easier with a consolidated, downloadable output.json log file, making it simple to review and share job details. If a transformation encounters an error and the ‘Skip on Error’ flag is off, the process will pause and allow you to resume after addressing the issue—giving you more control and reducing the risk of data

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - CSV to Delta
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcut Transformations - CSV to DeltaWith Fabric Shortcut Transformations, users can now seamlessly convert CSV files into Delta tables in their Lakehouse environment—no pipelines or complex ETL required. This feature enables always-in-sync data ingestion, automatically detecting and updating changes from source files. Users benefit from a simple, UI-driven experience that supports schema evolution, column mapping, and error handling, making it easy to manage both structured and semi-structured data. The system handles multiple CSV files, supports header and delimiter options, and is designe

fabricroadmap.title: Inbound network protection to OneLake with resource instance rules
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature offers a simple and secure way to restrict OneLake access to only your application's Azure resources, while blocking all other public access. It works by configuring resource instance rules specific to your designated Azure resource.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake Storage Lifecycle Management Policies
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake provides rule-based lifecycle management to help organizations optimize storage costs. These policies allow administrators to automatically transition data between hot, cool, and cold tiers based on last access or modification time.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake Storage Lifecycle Management Policies
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake provides rule-based lifecycle management to help organizations optimize storage costs. These policies allow administrators to automatically transition data between hot, cool, and cold tiers based on last access or modification time.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - file to table (content understanding)
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcut Transformations let you transform files to tables. With the instroduction of Content Understanding transform you can make any file a table.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security APIs for external engines
