fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake security allows seamless integration with 3rd party query engines through APIs for synchronizing security.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - ReadWrite permission - GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Configure write permissions for folders in a lakehouse using OneLake security. With this feature, viewers can be given selective write access to certain folders in the lakehouse enabling teams to write data without having Contributor or higher roles in the workspace.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - dynamic and multi-table RLS
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake security is adding support for dynamic and multi-table row level security. With dynamic RLS, users can create roles in OneLake that secure data differently for each user that queries the data. In addition, multi-table RLS allows data to be secured by querying values in a lookup table. Combined, these features empower users to complex RLS rules for securing enterprise data.

fabricroadmap.title: Onelake shortcuts to Azure Blob storage GA
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake blob shortcuts surface any container or folder from Azure Blob Storage inside Fabric as a normal OneLake path. The data stays where it is and is immediately queryable by Lakehouse, SQL, Spark, and Power BI. GA adds delegated credentials, workspace or service-principal auth, built-in caching for faster reads, and access through the on-premises data gateway.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut transform - parquet files to Delta table
fabricroadmap.summary: Parquet to Delta shortcut transform upgrades a Parquet shortcut into a Delta table. It builds the Delta transaction log and, when needed, rewrites data files to meet Delta specs, unlocking ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel for every Fabric engine.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut transform - JSON files to Delta table
fabricroadmap.summary: JSON to Delta shortcut transform reads JSON shortcuts, converts the data to Parquet.

fabricroadmap.title: SPN and Workspace Identity support for Dataverse shortcuts
fabricroadmap.summary: Dataverse shortcuts now honor service-principal and workspace-identity authentication, letting automated jobs and shared workspaces create and use shortcuts without personal tokens or manual consent.

fabricroadmap.title: Support Databricks workspaces behind private links
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric now connects to Azure Databricks workspaces secured with Azure Private Link.

fabricroadmap.title: Cache support for on-premises data gateway in OneLake shortcuts
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcut caching can be used to reduce egress costs associated with cross-cloud data access. As files are read through an external shortcut, the files are stored in a cache for the Fabric workspace. Subsequent read requests are served from cache rather than the remote storage provider. With the introduction of cache support for the On-premises-data gateway, you can leverage these capabilities while connecting to on-prem data or data behind a firewall.

fabricroadmap.title: CI/CD support for OneLake shortcuts
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric's lifecycle management tools provide a standardized system for communication and collaboration between all members of the development team throughout the life of the product.With the introduction of CI/CD support for OneLake shortcuts, you can easiliy manage your deployment of OneLake shortcuts across environments.

fabricroadmap.title: Easy management of orphaned OneLake shortcuts
fabricroadmap.summary: When people switch teams, leave the organization or lose certain access, your OneLake shortcuts can become unusable. With the new management capabilities of these orphaned shortcuts, you can easly restore your shortcuts with no business impact.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake catalog security management experience
fabricroadmap.summary: Today Fabric has many different UI experiences for managing permissions to data: the share dialog, the manage permissions page, workspace role settings, and other in-artifact code or role creation experiences. With the OneLake catalog secure tab, you can now manage all your OneLake security roles from a single location. Users can also view user access to workspaces, items, and domains to get an end-to-end picture of data access in Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security granular APIs
fabricroadmap.summary: In addition to the existing bulk API for managing OneLake security roles, we will add a new set of APIs for performing granular actions against roles.Examples include: create a single role, add a single member to a role, etc.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake data plane diagnostic events
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature logs OneLake data plane operations, such as reading or writing files, and stores them in a lakehouse of your choice. It captures detailed diagnostic logs for operations originating outside of Fabric (e.g. OneLake file explorer, Azure services). For operations inside Fabric (e.g. Fabric Spark, Fabric DW), the logs will enable you to connect to detailed information in the corresponding workload logs.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake encryption with customer-managed keys
fabricroadmap.summary: As part of our strategic roadmap to enhance data security and compliance, we are planning to introduce support for customer-managed keys (CMK) in OneLake. This feature provides organizations with greater control over their data encryption keys. With CMK, users will be able to manage their own encryption keys, ensuring that their data is protected in accordance with their specific security policies and regulatory requirements. If the customer's key is revoked, Microsoft will lose access to customer data in OneLake.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake Delta to Iceberg table virtualization
fabricroadmap.summary: Delta Lake tables in OneLake are automatically and virtually converted to the Apache Iceberg table format. This capability enhances interoperability of Fabric with your broader data and analytics environment. It allows you to seamlessly integrate your Fabric tables with services and engines that support the Apache Iceberg format. This includes Snowflake, as a major part of our [previously announced partnership](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-fabric/blog/2024/05/22/snowflake-and-microsoft-announce-expansion-of-their-partnership/). You can easily access and analyze your Fabric tables

fabricroadmap.title: Data Quality: Persist and Inspect Corrupt Rows in Shortcut Transformations
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcut Transformations today silently drops corrupt rows during file-to-Delta ingestion - users see a count of rejected rows in telemetry but have no way to inspect what failed, which file it came from, or when it was rejected. It's estimated that 35% of all jobs encounter corrupt rows that are silently discarded. This feature persists corrupt rows alongside valid data in the destination Delta table with source file path and ingestion timestamp, enabling direct inspection via SQL/Power BI, downstream remediation in silver-layer pipelines, and compliance audit trails. Opt-in via a simple feat

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake file explorer GA
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake file explorer will offer the full support that comes with Generally Availablity (GA). The OneLake file explorer application seamlessly integrates OneLake with Windows File Explorer. This application automatically syncs all OneLake items that you have access to in Windows File Explorer."Sync" refers to pulling up-to-date metadata on files and folders, and sending changes made locally to the OneLake service. Syncing doesn't download the data, it creates placeholders. You must double-click on a file to download the data locally.When you create, update, or delete a file via Windo

fabricroadmap.title: Add OneLake data to Foundry IQ Knowledge with OneLake catalog discovery experience
fabricroadmap.summary: We’re strengthening our better‑together story with Microsoft Foundry, making it easy to discover and build Knowledge directly from OneLake data through the OneLake catalog.Users can explore their entire OneLake data estate up front - viewing rich metadata, endorsements, sensitivity labels, and descriptions - and connect with a single click to add data to Knowledge.

fabricroadmap.title: Creation of Direct Lake semantic models in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI is standardizing on open-data formats by adopting Delta Lake and Parquet to help you avoid vendor lock-in and reduce data duplication. This minimizes data silos and fragmentation, offering a single source of truth across the enterprise. Direct Lake accelerates time to data-driven decisions by unlocking incredible performance directly against OneLake, without the need to manage costly, time-consuming data refreshes for large volumes of data in OneLake.Create Direct Lake semantic models from Power BI Desktop from any OneLake source, not only Lakehouse or Warehouse. This feature allows u

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot summary for subscriptions
fabricroadmap.summary: Subscriptions delivered to your email are a great way to ensure that you don't miss reports which help you drive your business. With copilot summaries in the email, we do the heavy lifting for you and deliver the most important insights so that you can focus on acting on the insights instead of deriving them. Copilot summaries are optional and can be added as a part of the subscription setup for new or existing subscriptions.

fabricroadmap.title: Create and run DAX queries with Query view in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: The DAX query view allows BI developers to create and run DAX queries in Power BI! Use the existing DAX query syntax to quickly query your data model.DAX expressions are used to define any measure, calculated column, calculated table, dynamic format string, calculation item, and row level security on your model. But that is not all you can do with DAX. With the DAX EVALUATE keyword, you can also use DAX to create a DAX query. This is much like a SQL query where you can specify columns and aggregations to return in a result table. You can learn more about DAX queries at DAX queries.This powerfu

fabricroadmap.title: Dynamic per recipient subscriptions
fabricroadmap.summary: With dynamic per recipient subscriptions, you can set up a single email subscription that delivers a different copy of a report to each recipient. Using data in a Power BI dataset, you can dynamically specify who should receive the subscription and with what data. For example, consider a multi-geo sales report. You can now send this report to all salespeople, with each receiving an email with an exported copy of the report with only sales data from their region. Support for dynamic subscriptions will be extended from only paginated reports to also include Power BI reports.

fabricroadmap.title: Deliver subscriptions to a OneDrive and SharePoint location
fabricroadmap.summary: With the ability to deliver Power BI and paginated report subscriptions to a OneDrive or SharePoint location, users can now view reports that are too large to be delivered to their inboxes. Accessing these reports from OneDrive or SharePoint locations makes finding reports easy too. Users can also keep all the historical reports that they need.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for measure descriptions
fabricroadmap.summary: Use Fabric Copilot for Power BI to create descriptions for your semantic model measures. The description property is important documentation for your measures, as only the measure name and description are available to those who are making reports from your semantic model. Fabric Copilot can make your semantic model documentation easier by generating measure descriptions for you. This is when you create the measure and when you update the DAX formula of a measure, at each stage Copilot can quickly generate or update the measure description, helping you maintain your documentation and maintainin

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for DAX query generation
fabricroadmap.summary: DAX query authors can use Copilot for DAX query generation to write, edit, or explain DAX queries on their model data. Ask what data you want to see returned and Copilot will give you the DAX query. Copilot can also be used to add a column or formatting to an existing DAX query, even finding the column in your data. Finally, Copilot can explain what a DAX query is doing or tell you more about specific DAX functions. This is a huge productivity boost in authoring DAX queries.

fabricroadmap.title: Organizational Apps for Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI apps are one of the easiest ways to package up and securely distribute Power BI reporting to your organization in a customized and easy-to-use experience. Previously one Power BI app could be created per workspace. With apps rebuilt for Fabric, multiple organizational apps can be created per workspace. Apps can contain more than just Power BI items like reports, but Fabric items like notebooks too. And the app experience can be customized in new ways with more control over the color (choose any color), navigation style, and landing experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Live edit of Direct Lake semantic models in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Previously, you could only create and edit semantic models using the incredible query performance of Direct Lake for your lakehouse based reports from the Power BI service. With live edit of Direct Lake semantic models in Power BI Desktop, you can also edit these semantic models in Power BI Desktop. Access the full power of semantic modeling capabilities and Git integration provided by Power BI Desktop for Direct Lake models! You can live edit semantic models by selecting the semantic model in OneLake Data Hub and simply click “Edit”.

fabricroadmap.title: XMLA endpoint support for service principal profiles
fabricroadmap.summary: Service principal profiles (SPPs) allow ISVs to build scalable applications that enable better customer data isolation and establish tighter security boundaries between customers. We have heard from customers that lack of XMLA support for SPPs limit the ability of ISVs to meet the requirements of their customers for more advanced BI solutions. With XMLA-based support for SPPs, ISVs can enable their customers to work with 3rd-party tools, automation scripts, and other solutions that rely on XMLA.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot in Power BI Mobile apps
fabricroadmap.summary: Helping the on th go user to get immidiate answers to their data questions but asking Copilot data questions directly from their mobile app. Helping the users to uncover insights that exist in the model, but might not always be visible in the visuals on the report, or just hard to understand from the mobile form factor.

fabricroadmap.title: NFC Support in Power BI Mobile apps
fabricroadmap.summary: Integrating Power BI Mobile apps with NFC card, to enable organizations to make Power BI reports easily accessible for their frontline workers, who work in various places and need quick access to data for making informative decisions. Using the Power BI Mobile app, user can configure an NFC card with any Power BI item. Later, other employees can use their mobile app to see this report just by tapping the same NFC card.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot in Power BI
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot in Power BI brings advanced generative AI to experiences across Power BI report creation and consumption experiences. Copilot assists users to create new report pages by providing suggestions on how to analyze their data. It can also automatically create, format, and lay out visuals based on their natural language requests. Further, users can chat with Copilot in order to update and refine their report designs and to learn about the data presented in visuals. And most importantly, with Copilot the user is always in control. They decide what to keep, modify, or discard, and their data a

fabricroadmap.title: Narrative with Copilot in Power BI
fabricroadmap.summary: Report creators in Power BI can use the new Narrative with Copilot visual to add generative AI summaries of their data within reports. Copilot provides suggested prompts that are used to summarize and find insights in data. Optionally, report creators can customize these prompts to fine tune the language, scope, and formatting of generated summaries. All insights generated by Copilot include citations that describe the sourced report data. Copilot summaries automatically regenerate when filters change, and they enforce any Power BI data security (like row-level security).

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for DAX query generation
fabricroadmap.summary: DAX query authors can use Copilot for DAX query generation to write, edit, or explain DAX queries on their model data. Ask what data you want to see returned and Copilot will give you the DAX query. Copilot can also be used to add a column or formatting to an existing DAX query, even finding the column in your data. Finally, Copilot can explain what a DAX query is doing or tell you more about specific DAX functions. This is a huge productivity boost in authoring DAX queries.

fabricroadmap.title: Combine existing mapping visuals into one with Azure Maps
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers will get the best features of all mapping visuals rolled into a single visual. The new mapping visual supports the use of shapes, points, shading, and adding more data points than the current default map visual.

fabricroadmap.title: Control visual formatting with improved capabilities
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI will add new formatting capabilities that will provide users with more control over the appearance of their visuals. New format options will allow setting the padding and margins of visuals, and their default values will apply good design practices that will result in appealing visuals.

fabricroadmap.title: Create reports in the Power BI service with new data sources
fabricroadmap.summary: It will be possible to create new reports in the Power BI service by using over 100 connectors and 300 transformations, supported by the full capability of Power Query Online.

fabricroadmap.title: Automatic mobile report layout in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI Desktop already supports creating an alternative report layout that’s optimized for mobile devices. However, the mobile layout is a blank canvas, which requires the report creator to add, size, and format visuals. To increase productivity, a new experience will automatically generate the mobile layout by selecting a button. Report creators can accept this layout as the final design, or they can use it as their starting point.

fabricroadmap.title: Visual calculations
fabricroadmap.summary: A visual calculation is a DAX calculation that's defined and executed directly on a visual. Visual calculations make it easier to create calculations that were previously hard to create, leading to simpler DAX, easier maintenance, and better performance. See [Using visual calculations](/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-visual-calculations-overview).

fabricroadmap.title: Author calculation groups
fabricroadmap.summary: Calculation groups are a simple way to reduce the number of measures in a model by grouping common measure expressions. Calculation groups work with existing explicit DAX measures by automating repetitive patterns. For example, a sales analyst might want to view sales and order quantities by month-to-date (MTD), quarter-to-date (QTD), year-to-date (YTD), orders year-to-date for the previous year (PY), and so on.Calculation groups are supported by Power BI models, however they’re an engine-only feature. With this enhancement, data modelers will be able to create calculation groups by using Powe

fabricroadmap.title: Create and run DAX queries with Query view in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Professional BI developers can write and run DAX queries natively within Power BI. Previously, as DAX queries is an existing feature, a BI developer would have needed to use third party external tools or use an API in order to write and run DAX queries. Now, they can write and run DAX queries natively in Power BI in context and with additional tools to quickly get started and productively use DAX queries.

fabricroadmap.title: Periodic refresh in Power BI Storytelling add-in to support Slideshow
fabricroadmap.summary: A Microsoft PowerPoint presentation can be configured to run in a continuous loop. This can be useful for general data displays, kiosks, or any other informational display that will run with or without interaction.We are adding a setting to Power BI add-in that will tell the add-in to automatically refresh the data in the slide every configured interval, so when the presentation is set for a continuous loop, the data keeps updating showing the most recent insights.

fabricroadmap.title: Enhancing image capture in Power BI add-in for PowerPoint
fabricroadmap.summary: Previously, when users add Power BI report or visual to a PowerPoint presentation using the Power BI add-in, Power BI checks the user permissions before presenting any live data to those who view the presentation. But if the add-in was set as image, and when PowerPoint uses screen capture as a thumbnail, there is no check on who the user is. In this update we will allow users to tell PowerPoint whether to show the image to every user who has access to the presentation or to limit that only to those who have access to the report in Power BI. In addition, the default thumbnail will be disabled.

fabricroadmap.title: Dynamic per recipient subscriptions
fabricroadmap.summary: With dynamic per recipient subscriptions, you can set up a single email subscription that delivers a different copy of a report to each recipient. Using data in a Power BI dataset, you can dynamically specify who should receive the subscription and with what data. For example, consider a multi-geo sales report. You can now send this report to all salespeople, with each receiving an email with an exported copy of the report with only sales data from their region. Support for dynamic subscriptions will be extended from only paginated reports to also include Power BI reports.

fabricroadmap.title: Customize content access request messages for Power BI organizational apps
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature will allow setting a custom entry point for each Power BI organizational app to an organization's internal access management system from Power BI Access Request messages. This feature will be especially useful for organizations that rely on security groups to control access to content.

fabricroadmap.title: Manage access to hidden content and link to content in Power BI organizational apps
fabricroadmap.summary: A new setting will allow organizational app creators to propagate access to an app’s hidden content to app users. In addition to improved control over access propagation, app creators will be able to copy links to content in apps from the app edit experience. The hidden content setting and ability to grab links to content give app creators control over the app navigation experience they have been asking for.

fabricroadmap.title: Balance user queries with query scale-out GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Query scale-out is a Power BI Premium feature that load balances user queries across multiple dataset read replicas in a pool of Power BI Premium nodes. Essentially, it speeds up query response times for high user-concurrency workloads. Additionally, dataset refresh operations benefit from increased isolation from the read replicas that protect user queries and improve performance.The management of query scale-out in Power BI is highly automated compared to other platforms, such as Azure Analysis Services. Also, adding and removing read replicas is performed dynamically based on live usage.

fabricroadmap.title: Stored credentials for Direct Lake dataset security in Microsoft Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: By default, Direct Lake storage mode accesses data in a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse or warehouse by using single sign-on (SSO). With SSO, the credentials of the user interacting with the Power BI report (or XMLA client tool) must have permission to query the underlying lakehouse or warehouse.However, it’s possible to use stored credentials, in which case the dataset owner can disable SSO. That means end users don’t require permission to query the underlying lakehouse or warehouse, and data security can be set up in the Power BI dataset. Direct Lake datasets can implement dataset data security,

fabricroadmap.title: Connect to new datasources and create paginated reports on PBI Report Builder
fabricroadmap.summary: You can create print-ready paginated reports from PBI Report Builder from datasources such as Snowflake and Databricks without requiring ODBC. You can then publish and share these reports on Power BI service.

fabricroadmap.title: Author calculation groups in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Calculation groups provide a simple way to reduce the number of measures in a model by grouping common measure expressions. Calculation groups work with existing explicit DAX measures by automating repetitive patterns. For example, a sales analyst might want to view sales and order quantities by month-to-date (MTD), quarter-to-date (QTD), year-to-date (YTD), orders year-to-date for the previous year (PY), and so on. With this enhancement, data modelers will be able to create calculation groups by using Power BI Desktop.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Power BI (Semantic Models)
fabricroadmap.summary: Workspace admins responsible for safeguarding organizational data will be able to leverage Outbound Access Control (OAP) in Fabric to ensure that Semantic Models and Power BI Reports are permitted to connect only to explicitly approved data sources. OAP helps to prevent data exfiltration by blocking data connections to unapproved or potentially risky endpoints, thereby enforcing organizational data governance and compliance requirements.

fabricroadmap.title: Button slicer
fabricroadmap.summary: In Power BI, the button slicer is an interactive visual allowing users to filter data in reports, providing an easy and dynamic way to scope down your other visuals.Among the various types of slicers, the button slicer stands. Button slicer offers customizable button styles, interactive states, conditional formatting for labels, and a grid layout for arranging buttons in rows and columns. Additionally, the button slicer can integrate images, enhancing visual appeal and providing more context.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot in Fabric for Power BI is now Generally available. This capability allows report authors to quickly and easily create brand new reports using the natural language to express intent. Copilot will take the intent and will quickly convert it to a brand new report page consisting of visuals, measures and filters automatically layed out by Copilot.

fabricroadmap.title: Dark mode support in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allows users to toggle dark mode insiode Power BI Desktop

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot answer questions
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allows users to ask questions against their data model using Copilot even if the answer is not currently within the report

fabricroadmap.title: Visual improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: We are continiously making a ton of improvement in the core visuls space and in this upcomming update we will be working on several of your top items including: Layout options for the matrix visual Reference layer enhancements for the Azure Maps visual Improved legends for cartesian charts More flexible markers for line and scatter charts A completely revamped list slicer

fabricroadmap.title: Model explorer provides easy navigation to author objects
fabricroadmap.summary: The model explorer provides a convenient tree view of all the semantic model objects in the Data pane. The semantic model is all the metadata about your data, and it impacts how your data shows in reports and DAX queries. Model explorer shows all the semantic model items at-a-glance. Find items fast with the search. Focus on what you want to do by expanding and collapsing different item sections. Know how many of each item you have with counts on each section. Semantic model: Clicking on the top semantic model node shows a properties pane with semantic model settings such as discourage implici

fabricroadmap.title: Table and matrix fixed width columns
fabricroadmap.summary: A new option in the Table and Matrix visuals to specify each columns width.

fabricroadmap.title: Table visual custom totals
fabricroadmap.summary: Options to add a custom total in a table visual.

fabricroadmap.title: Modeling Copilot
fabricroadmap.summary: Creators in Fabric can easily improve their semantic models with Copilot. Powered by Power BI Modeling MCP, you will be able to leverage AI to modify semantic model to meet new requirements for reporting, including but optiming your semantic model for AI.

fabricroadmap.title: Agent Skill for Power BI Reports
fabricroadmap.summary: With the agent skill for Power BI reports, AI tools can now more easily interact with Power BI’s reporting layer. This powerful skill will allow report creation from scratch based on requirements, updating the report theme based on requirements, ormodifying visual and report elements.

fabricroadmap.title: Matrix expand and collapse icons on column headers
fabricroadmap.summary: Adding expand and collapse icons to the column headers when more than one column is added, like how there are expand and collapse icons for row headers when there are more than one row added to the matrix in Power BI.

fabricroadmap.title: Donut Chart - Center Value
fabricroadmap.summary: Display a total, custom measure, or label directly in the center of donut charts, eliminating the need for overlaying a separate card visual. The center value responds to filters, selections, and scales automatically across all platforms.

fabricroadmap.title: Card Visual - Trend Chart
fabricroadmap.summary: Display a built-in trend chart (line or column) inside Card visuals to show how values change over time. No SVGs or extra visuals needed.

fabricroadmap.title: Visuals categorical axis "scroll starts from" option (scroll from right)
fabricroadmap.summary: Formatting pane options for where the scroll bar starts from when visible on the axis of a visual. For example, if I have a line chart showing trends over time, I can set this to scroll from right and when viewers open the report the latest data points show first and they can scroll to the left to see the historical trend.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake file URLs for report visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Reference OneLake files directly in your report visuals for images and maps.

fabricroadmap.title: Modern visual defaults and customizing theme improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: New visual defaults to overhaul the Power BI base report theme to create professional looking reports in seconds. This update incorporates many of the latest updates we have made to reports and report theming. This update also includes increasing the default page size to 1080x1920. Report theme customizaton improvements such as color palettes and custom theme authoring from the formatting pane available in both Desktop and web.

fabricroadmap.title: Chat with your data experience in the Power BI Mobile apps
fabricroadmap.summary: Chat with your data in the Power BI Mobile app lets you ask questions in natural language and instantly get answers from your reports and semantic models. It uses Copilot intelligence to deliver insights, summaries, and visuals right from your mobile device, so you can explore data and make decisions on the go.

fabricroadmap.title: Image visual improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: The Image visual improvements empower report creators to craft more engaging experiences for report consumers. Report creators can easily maintain image visuals with more image formatting options, more image source options, and the ability to change the image in-place.

fabricroadmap.title: New Card visual
fabricroadmap.summary: The new Card visual brings a modern and visually engaging way to highlight key measures in your reports, now with support for hero images, new default styling, and consistent formatting experience. This card can be used with one or more measures, including additional measures for complete context. For example, you can show your sales measure with supporting details such as sales per day, change in sales, and units sold, all in a single card.

fabricroadmap.title: Matrix visual with auto-size columns
fabricroadmap.summary: A new option in the Matrix visual to automatically distribute columns to fit the width of the visual container. No more manually resizing each column to fill the gap.

fabricroadmap.title: Modern tooltips on report visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Updated styling to match a report theme on tooltips on Power BI report visuals. Modern tooltips also include drill down and drill through actions.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure map visual markers
fabricroadmap.summary: Customize markers in Azure map visual. Use new icons or your own images with more formatting options to make your map ready for reports.

fabricroadmap.title: Input slicer visual (previously called Text slicer)
fabricroadmap.summary: The input slicer visual lets you type in values and search to filter a text data column, or type in values for a Fabric user data function with the new translytical task flow in Power BI reports.

fabricroadmap.title: Modern visual defaults and customizing theme improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: New visual defaults to overhaul the Power BI base report theme to create professional looking reports in seconds. This update incorporates many of the latest updates we have made to reports and report theming. This update also includes increasing the default page size to 1080x1920. Report theme customizaton improvements such as color palettes and additional properties will be added during public preview.

fabricroadmap.title: Date picker slicer to set relative and manual date ranges
fabricroadmap.summary: Adds a date picker mode for date slicers so authors can pick a relative default range (e.g., “last full month”) that automatically rolls forward as time passes when published, without authors having to update the report each period. Report viewers can override it to filter to other relative ranges or any manual date range.

fabricroadmap.title: TMDL View in the Web
fabricroadmap.summary: We are bringing TMDL View in the web

fabricroadmap.title: Edit semantic models in the Power BI service GA
fabricroadmap.summary: For years, core modeling features like Power Query, relationship editing, and DAX authoring were only available in Power BI Desktop. These capabilities are now supported in the Power BI service as well, enabling you to build and manage semantic models directly in the browser. You can now add import tables from a variety of sources, shape data, define measures, manage relationships, configure row-level security, update model properties, and more, all without leaving the browser!

fabricroadmap.title: Centralized controller in Power BI integration with PowerPoint
fabricroadmap.summary: The Centralized controller in Power BI aims to enhance productivity for Power BI users who embed Power BI content in their PowerPoint presentations. This feature introduces a designated pane that provides a centralized location within the presentation, allowing users to execute an operation on all of the Power BI add-ins in the presentation with a sinlge click. This eliminates the need to manually update each slide, thereby streamlining the process of refreshing data and managing content across multiple slides. The Controller will offer various operations such as changing view modes, and refre

fabricroadmap.title: Translytical Task Flows
fabricroadmap.summary: Translytical task flows is a major evolution in Fabric that allows seamless insights to action on Power BI reports, such as updating customer records, adding annotations, and so much more!

fabricroadmap.title: Data point annotations in Power BI add-in for PowerPoint
fabricroadmap.summary: Annotations allow users to add descriptive text to a specific data point within a visualization. They serve as contextual explanations or highlights, aiding viewers in comprehending the visualization.Annotations benefits are:Enhanced Communication: Annotations aid in effectively communicating insights, explanations, or observations within the visualization itself, reducing the need for external documentation or additional explanations. Its main purpose is to highlight key insights, or mark data that need to be explained.Contextual Clarity: Annotations provide contextual information directly on

fabricroadmap.title: Semantic Link Notebook integration for Semantic Models
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing easily discoverable entry points for semantic link templates within Power BI. This enhancement will simplify leveraging the power of semantic link and notebooks by providing access to valuable templates like the Best Practice Analyzer and Memory Analyzer, with all configurations pre-set for you.

fabricroadmap.title: Power Query support for Import semantic models in the Web
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI users can now edit all core aspects of their import semantic models directly within the web, now including Power Query support. Users can add tables from various import sources, perform rich transformations using Power Query, refresh, manage relationships, define DAX measures, edit model properties, set row-level security roles, and more - all within the web model view without leaving the browser.

fabricroadmap.title: Direct Lake and Import composite models in the Web
fabricroadmap.summary: This capability will allow you to create semantic models that include both Direct Lake and import tables, providing flexibility with these storage modes. This type of composite semantic models can be created and edited directly in the web editing experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Power Query support for Import semantic models in the Web
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI users can now edit all core aspects of their import semantic models directly within the web, now including Power Query support. Users can add tables from various import sources, perform rich transformations using Power Query, refresh, manage relationships, define DAX measures, edit model properties, set row-level security roles, and more - all within the web model view without leaving the browser.

fabricroadmap.title: Connect to Power Query data sources and create paginated reports using PBI Report Builder
fabricroadmap.summary: Create print-ready paginated reports in Power BI Report Builder by connecting to over 100 data sources using the Get Data experience. You can transform and load Leverage parameterized, paginated reports functionality from PBI Report Builder with 100+ data sources by connecting using Power Query. Create pixel-perfect, print-ready paginated reports using data sources such as Snowflake and Databricks without requiring ODBC or an on-premises data gateway, and publish them to the Power BI service.

fabricroadmap.title: DirectQuery support for editing semantic models in the Power BI service
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature brings DirectQuery (DQ) support to Power BI web modeling, enabling users to create and edit DirectQuery and Dual models directly in the browser. Today, DirectQuery authoring is only available in Power BI Desktop.

fabricroadmap.title: Translytical task flows
fabricroadmap.summary: With translytical task flows, you can automate end-user actions like updating records, adding annotations, or creating workflows that trigger actions. Simply add a button in your Power BI report and link it to your Fabric user data function.

fabricroadmap.title: Visual calculations GA
fabricroadmap.summary: A visual calculation is a DAX calculation that's defined and executed directly on a visual. Visual calculations make it easier to create calculations previously hard to create, right in the visual.

fabricroadmap.title: Table auto-size columns
fabricroadmap.summary: A new option in the Table visual to automatically distribute columns to fit the width of the visual container. No more manually resizing each column to fill the gap.

fabricroadmap.title: Org Apps GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Org Apps allows you to easily create different apps for different pruposes with full source control support. In this upcomming release we will close alot of the most requested features and take Org Apps to General Availability.

fabricroadmap.title: Narrative Visual Support in PaaS embed
fabricroadmap.summary: This new capability will support the Narrative Visual in PaaS report embedding

fabricroadmap.title: Developer Mode GA
fabricroadmap.summary: We will be GAing developer mode in Desktop which will include the new PBIR format being default on for everyone. More details to follow.

fabricroadmap.title: Performance Analyzer in the Web
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature brings the current perf analyzer in the desktop accessible inside the Web

fabricroadmap.title: DAX User Defined Functions
fabricroadmap.summary: User-Defined Functions (UDFs) allow you to encapsulate reusable, parameterized DAX logic into named functions that can be called across measures, calculated columns, and visual calculations throughout your semantic model. UDFs support both value and expression parameters, enabling you to centralize complex business logic—like tax calculations or currency conversions—so it's written once and maintained in a single place. Functions can be created in DAX Query View or TMDL View and appear as first-class objects under a dedicated "Functions" node in Model Explorer

fabricroadmap.title: TMDL View
fabricroadmap.summary: TMDL View offers a "semantic modeling as code" experience with Tabular Model Definition Language (TMDL) within Power BI Desktop. It enables users to script, modify, and apply changes to semantic model objects in a modern code editor, significantly enhancing user efficiency. Future updates will integrate Copilot for handling time-intensive tasks such as model translations, documentation, bulk operations, among others.

fabricroadmap.title: Version history support for semantic models
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature aims to empower self-service users by providing confidence to recover from critical mistakes when editing semantic models on the web. Versions will be automatically captured in an Office-like version history pane for your web-edited Premium semantic models, allowing you to easily select and restore to any of these previous version of your semantic model. We plan to support Pro workspaces as well in a future release.

fabricroadmap.title: Web Modelling - Default on
fabricroadmap.summary: With this release, the data model editing in the web preview will be enabled by default for Premium workspaces. This allows Power BI users to modify existing semantic models on the web by editing relationships, creating DAX measures, and managing row-level security. We plan to support default on for Pro workspaces as well in a future release.

fabricroadmap.title: ALM support for Org Apps
fabricroadmap.summary: Introduce robust support for Application Lifecycle Management (ALM). The Public Preview of Org Apps will be updated to support change management via Git and can leverage Fabric Deployment Pipelines. This enables scenarios such as source control integration, version management, Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) for repeatable mission-critical deployments.

fabricroadmap.title: Audience support in Org Apps
fabricroadmap.summary: This improvement to Power BI's Org Apps will add support for defining user access and content display by audience(s), like the functionality in Power BI workspace apps. Audiences will allow for conditional display of content in the org app according to the audience or audiences a user belongs to. For instance, app creators can create one audience that can see only a subset of report within the app, but another audience with managerial oversite to make use of all of the reporting.

fabricroadmap.title: Semantic Link Notebook integration for Semantic Models
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing easily discoverable entry points for semantic link templates within Power BI. This enhancement will simplify leveraging the power of semantic link and notebooks by providing access to valuable templates like the Best Practice Analyzer and VertiPaq Analyzer, with all configurations pre-set for you.

fabricroadmap.title: XMLA endpoint support for service principal profiles
fabricroadmap.summary: Service principal profiles (SPPs) allow ISVs to build scalable applications that enable better customer data isolation and establish tighter security boundaries between customers. We have heard from customers that lack of XMLA support for SPPs limits the ability of ISVs to meet the requirements of their customers for more advanced BI solutions. With XMLA-based support for SPPs, ISVs can enable their customers to work with 3rd-party tools, automation scripts, and other solutions that rely on XMLA. For more information, see [Use service principal profiles to manage customer data in multitenant a

fabricroadmap.title: TMDL View
fabricroadmap.summary: TMDL View offers a "semantic modeling as code" experience with [Tabular Model Definition Language](/analysis-services/tmdl/tmdl-overview) (TMDL) within Power BI Desktop. It enables users to script, modify, and apply changes to semantic model objects in a modern code editor, significantly enhancing user efficiency. Future updates will integrate Copilot for handling time-intensive tasks such as model translations, documentation, bulk operations, among others.

fabricroadmap.title: Creation of Direct Lake semantic models in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Power BI is standardizing on open-data formats by adopting Delta Lake and Parquet to help you avoid vendor lock-in and reduce data duplication. This minimizes data silos and fragmentation, offering a single source of truth across the enterprise. Direct Lake accelerates time to data-driven decisions by unlocking incredible performance directly against OneLake, without the need to manage costly, time-consuming data refreshes for large volumes of data in OneLake.Create Direct Lake semantic models from Power BI Desktop from any OneLake source, not only Lakehouse or Warehouse. This feature allows u

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Power BI (Reports)
fabricroadmap.summary: Workspace admins responsible for safeguarding organizational data will be able to leverage Outbound Access Control (OAP) in Fabric to ensure that Semantic Models and Power BI Reports are permitted to connect only to explicitly approved data sources. OAP helps to prevent data exfiltration by blocking data connections to unapproved or potentially risky endpoints, thereby enforcing organizational data governance and compliance requirements.

fabricroadmap.title: Set as landing page in Power BI reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Always make sure your report viewers land on the right page

fabricroadmap.title: Tooltip options for Power BI visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Control which tooltips show and how the tooltips display on your visual

fabricroadmap.title: Shape map visual in Power BI reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Built-in shape map support coming with topojson, geojson, and URL support

fabricroadmap.title: Input slicer numeric support
fabricroadmap.summary: Input slicer to allow numeric data colors for filtering and forced numeric entry.

fabricroadmap.title: Conditional formatting for lines and series/labels in Power BI visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Conditional formatting to be available for series in Power BI visuals. This includes lines, markers, and legends.

fabricroadmap.title: List slicer with dropdown mode
fabricroadmap.summary: List slicer with drop down mode and advanced search options.

fabricroadmap.title: Gantt chart visual
fabricroadmap.summary: A new core visual in Power BI -- the gantt chart, visualizing all your product tasks in a Power BI report.

fabricroadmap.title: Add to preset for Power BI visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Take the formatting on an individual visual and add it to the custom report theme for re-use on other visuals in the same report or a new report.

fabricroadmap.title: Organizational themes for Power BI reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Organizational themes (preview) allow Power BI administrators to centrally manage and distribute custom report themes across the organization. Maintaining a consistent visual identity across Power BI reports is now simpler and more scalable, thanks to organizational themes. Whether reports are built manually or generated with Copilot, this feature ensures that styling and branding stay aligned with your organization's identity and design standards.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream reference data join with one lake delta tables
fabricroadmap.summary: The Reference Data Join feature in Eventstream enables you to enrich streaming events by joining them with static or slowly changing delta tables in one lake.User can reference any one lake delta tables using lakehouse, and join it with streaming data in eventstream to enahace and add additional context to their events during processing.

fabricroadmap.title: AzMonStream data format in Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Eventhouse now supports the [AzMonStream data format](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/ingestion-supported-formats?view=microsoft-fabric).This data format allows you to ingest data emitted by Azure Monitor diagnostic settings sent to Azure Event Hub directly. No Update Policy are required to expend each record in the payload array: this is all taken care of by the data format!This data format will also soon be supported in the Get Data experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Service Bus source connector for Eventstream
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream now provides a generally available Azure Service Bus source connector. Customers can bring messages from Service Bus queues and topics into Microsoft Fabric for real-time processing without custom code.With this capability, you can:- Connect Eventstream to Azure Service Bus queues and topics.- Route Service Bus data to Fabric destinations for analysis and alerts.

fabricroadmap.title: Map
fabricroadmap.summary: A low-code, no-code experience enabling users to create and consume map-centric applications that analyze and visualize data in time and space. It integrates Real-Time Intelligence with data enrichment and processing of geospatial data.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream Connector: Oracle DB CDC
fabricroadmap.summary: The Oracle CDC connector for Eventstream captures database changes from Oracle Database and streams them into Eventstream for real-time processing and analysis.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream Connector: MQTTv3
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream now supports MQTT protocol versions v3 and v5, enabling you to connect to an MQTT broker, subscribe to specific topics, and stream data from those topics directly into Eventstream for real-time processing.

fabricroadmap.title: VNET/On-Prem support for Eventstream Connectors
fabricroadmap.summary: The Eventstream streaming connector in Fabric Real-Time Intelligence enables the ingestion of real-time data from various sources into Fabric. This VNET/On-Prem support feature extends the streaming source’s environment from public networks to private networks, such as cloud virtual networks or on-premises networks.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream Managed Private Endpoint Support for Azure Event Hubs & IoT Hub Sources
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream integration with Managed Private Endpoint for Azure EH and IoT Hub sourcesManaged Private Endpoint is a network security feature of the Fabric platform that allows Fabric items to securely access data sources behind a firewall or not accessible from the public internet. By integrating Eventstream with the Managed Private Endpoint, allowing you to securely connect to your Azure resources within a private network.

fabricroadmap.title: No-code creation and edit experience for Eventhouse tables
fabricroadmap.summary: No-code creation and edit experience for Eventhouse tables

fabricroadmap.title: Sample Gallery at Semantic Model page
fabricroadmap.summary: Learn RTI end-to-end experience with sample gallery for new and existing customers at PBI semantic model page

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time Dashboard
fabricroadmap.summary: A dashboard is a collection of tiles, optionally organized in pages, where each tile has an underlying query and a visual representation. Natively export Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries to a dashboard as visuals and later modify their underlying queries and visual formatting as needed. In addition to ease of data exploration, this fully integrated dashboard experience provides improved query and visualization performance with light, flexible modeling on high granularity low latency data.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream data preprocessing to KQL database destination
fabricroadmap.summary: The addition of the KQL database destination with data transformation enables customers to transform, enrich, and reduce the data volume before it's routed to KQL databases.

fabricroadmap.title: Improved Get Data experience
fabricroadmap.summary: Users experience a simplified and improved Get Data experience to get their data into a KQL database.

fabricroadmap.title: Co-pilot for Real-Time Intelligence
fabricroadmap.summary: Co-pilot allows you to write queries in natural language and have them translated into Kusto Query Language (KQL). You can use Co-pilot to ask your how-to queries, explore your data in a KQL database, and create Kusto entities such as tables, functions, and materialized views.

fabricroadmap.title: New eventstream destination to Data Activator
fabricroadmap.summary: The Data Activator destination option helps customers route events to Data Activator, where they can build triggers based on the event data from eventstreams natively.

fabricroadmap.title: Create actions and alerts over Eventhouse data with Data Activator
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature provides a low-code/no-code experience to drive actions and alerts from your KQL database data presented in a Real-Time Dashboard. Data Activator gives you a single place to define actionable patterns in your data. These patterns can range from simple thresholds (such as a value being exceeded) to more complex patterns over time (such a value trending down). When Data Activator detects an actionable pattern, it triggers an action. That action can be an email or a Teams alert to the relevant person in your organization. It can also trigger an automatic process, via a Power Automate

fabricroadmap.title: Pause, stop, or restart eventstream flows
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature offers customers the capability to pause, stop, or restart real-time event flows, so they can iterate on transformation or event flow logic during the development phase.

fabricroadmap.title: Autoscale eventstreams
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature provides the flexibility to automatically scale capacity in response to event data traffic volume, enabling seamless improvement of eventstream throughput without disrupting your business operations.

fabricroadmap.title: Notebook integration
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can natively query KQL databases from Microsoft Fabric notebooks. Use notebooks to run queries on KQL databases, save the resulting data frames, ingest data into KQL databases, and more.

fabricroadmap.title: Delta support to the KQL database OneLake representation
fabricroadmap.summary: KQL database data is already available in OneLake in parquet format. Adding Delta support enables other Fabric capabilities to use the OneLake presence as a table rather than as a list of files.

fabricroadmap.title: Administrative monitoring
fabricroadmap.summary: You can use administrative monitoring to search audit logs, and to track usage and adoption, capacity consumption, and availability.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Synapse Link from Cosmos DB to Fabric Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Users can stream all changes from Cosmos DB to a Fabric Eventhouse KQL database, enabling large scale, powerful analytics via Eventstream Cosmos DB CDC. /fabric/real-time-intelligence/event-streams/add-source-azure-cosmos-db-change-data-capture /fabric/real-time-intelligence/get-data-eventstream

fabricroadmap.title: Improved no-code stream processing designer
fabricroadmap.summary: Users have an improved eventstream editing experience, with more intuitive gestures in the no-code designer.

fabricroadmap.title: "Get data from Eventstream" in multiple Fabric items
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers are able to get event data from eventstreams in multiple Fabric items, including Lakehouse, KQL Database, and Reflex.

fabricroadmap.title: Cloud connection creation embedded in eventstreams
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can create a cloud connection directly within their eventstreams, without navigating to another webpage.

fabricroadmap.title: Enhanced Custom App Details tab offers comprehensive endpoint information
fabricroadmap.summary: The Details tab of the Custom App source and destination offers comprehensive information about the eventstream endpoint. Available information includes connection strings in Kafka, Eventhub, and AMQP formats, as well as sample Java code for event ingestion and consumption using these three protocols.

fabricroadmap.title: Scale up to 100 MB/s for eventstream processing
fabricroadmap.summary: An eventstream can support events ingestion throughput up to 100 MB/s while ingesting data to KQL databases and lakehouses.

fabricroadmap.title: Two ingestion modes for eventstream lakehouse destinations
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream lakehouse destinations support two ingestion modes: low latency and high throughput.

fabricroadmap.title: Table optimization shortcut in eventstream lakehouse destinations
fabricroadmap.summary: The table optimization shortcut helps users by opening a notebook with a Spark job that compacts small streaming files in the lakehouse table.

fabricroadmap.title: Content-based event routing to destinations in eventstreams
fabricroadmap.summary: Bringing the no-code event processor to the eventstream main canvas allows customers to route event data to their destinations based on event content, using event processing logic defined with the event processor.

fabricroadmap.title: Customizable event data retention in eventstreams
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers have the flexibility to set the event data retention time, ensuring that event data is retained in their eventstreams according to their specific business requirements.

fabricroadmap.title: CI/CD support for Eventstream items
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can easily version and deploy their eventstreams across development, testing, and production workspaces using the integrated Git integration and deployment experience in the Fabric platform.

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time Dashboards General Availability
fabricroadmap.summary: General availability of Fabric Real-Time Dashboards

fabricroadmap.title: Data Exploration General Availability
fabricroadmap.summary: General availability of no-code data exploration experiences for Real-Time Intelligence, including the ability to explore real-time dashboards tile data and query results.

fabricroadmap.title: Copilot for Real-Time Intelligence
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot for Real-Time Intelligence is an advanced AI tool designed to help you explore your data and extract valuable insights. You can input questions about your data, which are then automatically translated into Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries. Copilot streamlines the process of analyzing data for both experienced KQL users and citizen data scientists.

fabricroadmap.title: Real time dashboard in Fabric OrgApps
fabricroadmap.summary: Org apps support for Real time dashboards

fabricroadmap.title: Create Real time dashboards with Copilot
fabricroadmap.summary: Auto create Real-Time Dashboard for KQL tables, including metadata tiles and insights tiles generated by Copilot

fabricroadmap.title: Multivariate Anomaly Detection
fabricroadmap.summary: The Azure Anomaly Detector multi variate technology will be natively available in Fabric. Train the detector using spark and notebooks or using Eventhouses, and use it to detect anomalies in real time as new data arrives.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse ALM Support
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventhouse ALM Support to allow for automatic deployments via Git Integration, Deployment Pipelines, and API with Definition.

fabricroadmap.title: New streaming connector for Azure Service Bus
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can leverage new connector to bring the streaming events from Azure Service Bus to Eventstream.

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time hub left-navigation consolidation for Data Sources
fabricroadmap.summary: To improve clarity and task completion in Real Time hub, we’re streamlining the left navigation. Users have reported confusion due to multiple overlapping entry points, making it difficult to locate the right actions for their real-time data workflows. By consolidating and simplifying the left-navigation menu, we aim to reduce cognitive load and help users quickly identify the most relevant entry point for their tasks.

fabricroadmap.title: Get data from Real-Time Hub within Data Activator
fabricroadmap.summary: Bring new events into reflex items by using the embedded Real-Time Hub browser.

fabricroadmap.title: Create triggers from Real-Time Hub
fabricroadmap.summary: Across the Real-Time Hub you'll see options to create new triggers and alerts on both business and system events.

fabricroadmap.title: Taking action through Fabric Items
fabricroadmap.summary: Reflex items will support starting Fabric item jobs as an action. You'll be able to kick off data pipelines and notebooks.

fabricroadmap.title: Set Alerts on KQL Querysets
fabricroadmap.summary: Data Activator will be able to monitor the results of queries managed in a KQL Queryset, running the query on a regular schedule and acting on the results.

fabricroadmap.title: More trigger options
fabricroadmap.summary: To address further requests for monitoring different business conditions, Data Activator will support triggers that check date/time values, basic math functions etc.

fabricroadmap.title: Low latency triggers
fabricroadmap.summary: We hear in customer feedback that triggers need to react faster when the specified condition is met. Data Activator will support lower-latency triggers in scenarios with simple conditions and lower volumes of data.This feature will be Private Preview in this time frame.

fabricroadmap.title: Support for parameters in triggering Fabric actions
fabricroadmap.summary: Rules that take action by starting Fabric jobs (notebooks or pipelines) will be able to pass the value of properties in the activator model as parameters to the job.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventhouse, a cutting-edge database workspace meticulously crafted to manage and store event-based data, is now officially available for general use. With Eventhouse, users can perform high-performance analysis of big data and real-time data querying, processing billions of events within seconds. The platform allows users to organize data into compartments (databases) within one logical item, facilitating efficient data management. Additionally, Eventhouse enables the sharing of compute and cache resources across databases, maximizing resource utilization.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse OneLake Availability
fabricroadmap.summary: Enabling data availability of Eventhouse in OneLake means that customers can enjoy the best of both worlds: they can query the data with high performance and low latency in their Eventhouse and query the same data in Delta Lake format via any other Fabric engines such as Power BI Direct Lake mode, Warehouse, Lakehouse, Notebooks, and more.

fabricroadmap.title: Create a database shortcut to another KQL Database
fabricroadmap.summary: A database shortcut in Eventhouse is an embedded reference to a source database. The database shortcut is attached in read-only mode, making it possible to view and run queries on the data that was ingested into the source KQL Database without ingesting it. This helps with data sharing scenarios where you can share data in-place either within teams, or even with external customers.

fabricroadmap.title: Support for AI Anomaly Detector
fabricroadmap.summary: AI Anomaly Detector algorithms are supported in Microsoft Fabric, allowing for real time scoring by KQL with inline Python in Real-Time Intelligence.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse tenant level private endpoint support
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can increase their network security by limiting access to Eventhouse at a tenant-level, from one or more virtual networks (VNets) via private links. This will prevent unauthorized access from public networks and only permit data plane operations from specific VNets.

fabricroadmap.title: New experience for data exploration from Real-Time Dashboards
fabricroadmap.summary: Directly from a real-time dashboard, users can refine their exploration using a user-friendly, form-like interface. This intuitive and dynamic experience is tailored for insights explorers craving insights based on real-time data. Add filters, create aggregations, and switch visualization types without writing queries to easily uncover insights.

fabricroadmap.title: Use Real-Time hub to Get Data in KQL Database in Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: With Real-Time hub embedded in KQL Database experience, each user in the tenant can view and add streams which they have access and directly ingest it to a KQL Database table in Eventhouse.

fabricroadmap.title: Activator performance & scale improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: Activator items will support up to 1000 events per second per stream, and activations typically happen within 30 seconds of the event being received.

fabricroadmap.title: Activator alerts on Power BI, KQL Queryset and Real-Time Dashboard
fabricroadmap.summary: Activator will support monitoring data from Power BI reports, Querysets, and Real-Time Dashboards. You set up an alert and configure it in a side pane.

fabricroadmap.title: "Get Events" from Activator
fabricroadmap.summary: From within an activator item, you choose ‘Get data’ to pull events from Real-Time Hub. You get search and catalog capabilities over all streams in your organization, and can connect to external sources with connectors to streams, change data capture feeds and more.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric item job actions
fabricroadmap.summary: Activator lets you start Fabric items as an action. For example, you can run a Fabric pipeline when files are created in Azure data lake storage. Fabric pipelines and Spark notebooks are supported.

fabricroadmap.title: Maximum number of rule actions
fabricroadmap.summary: To avoid overloading messaging systems and generating too much noise, Activator has limits on how many times a rule can send an email/Teams message or trigger a Power Automate flow. This stops users being flooded with messages.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Monitoring integration
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Workspace Monitoring is designed to provide a seamless and consistent monitoring experience with end-to-end visibility across all Fabric items. Workspace Monitoring is based on the Real-time Intelligence Eventhouse KQL database. Once Fabric Monitoring is enabled, a KQL database is created to store all the workspace items event logs. KQL databases are ideal for time series logs and metrics monitoring solutions.

fabricroadmap.title: Power BI alert management
fabricroadmap.summary: Users will be able to see and manage all alerts configured with Activator alerts on their current Power BI report. Choosing ‘Set alert’ for a report will present a list of all the alerts that you set up on that report, giving you the option to add new ones, start or stop rules, or delete them if they’re no longer necessary.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream to Activator Destination GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Activator can monitor and act on events ingested to Fabric through an Eventstream. This feature is to track GA of this destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Activator delay tolerance controls
fabricroadmap.summary: Streams of events often arrive out-of-order. When comparing the change between a new event and the previous one, customers ask for control over how long to wait before ignoring late arriving events. This affects the overall latency of the rule, but allows users the manage the tradeoff between speed and accuracy.

fabricroadmap.title: Migration from Synapse Data Explorer pools to Fabric Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Seamless migration from Synapse Data Explorer pools to Fabric Eventhouse.

fabricroadmap.title: Query Acceleration over OneLake Delta Tables
fabricroadmap.summary: Running queries on shortcuts is typically slow due to various factors such as network calls to fetch data from storage, the absence of indexes, and more. Customers who are used to running performant queries on top of ingested data in Eventhouse, will be able to gain similar performance by caching Delta tables with query acceleration .

fabricroadmap.title: Enhancements to Event processor in Eventstream
fabricroadmap.summary: This includes three enhancements. First, personalize operation nodes and easily filter out 'null' values from your data. Second, manage and rename your column fields easily in the Aggregate operation. Third, Change your values to different data types using the Manage Fields operation .

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time Hub for all data in motion GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Real-Time hub is the single estate for all data-in-motion across your entire organization.

fabricroadmap.title: Get events experience in Real-Time Hub (change to explain value or remove for 18/24)
fabricroadmap.summary: Whether data is coming from new or existing sources, streams, or available events, the Get Events experience allows users to connect to a wide range of sources directly from Real-Time hub, Eventstreams, Eventhouse and Data Activator.

fabricroadmap.title: New streaming connectors including Confluent Kafka, AWS Kinesis, PostgresSQL CDC and more
fabricroadmap.summary: Beyond Microsoft sources, users can now stream data from other platforms like Google Cloud, Amazon Kinesis, Database change data capture streams, etc. using our new messaging connectors. Our messaging connectors are powered by Kafka connect with Camel Kafka connectors that offer a pluggable, declarative data integration framework, and flexibility for diverse source connections on popular data platforms, as well as the Debezium that could connect databases for fetching the Change Data Capture (CDC) streams.

fabricroadmap.title: New sources of discrete events from Fabric system events and Azure storage events
fabricroadmap.summary: Discrete events (a.k.a. notification events) are significant (important) facts that have happened, and that trigger state changes or actions in the downstream consumer applications (subscribers). Examples include events like OrderPlaced in order system, blob storage changes in Azure sources, or item changes in Fabric system.

fabricroadmap.title: Source from Real-Time Hub in Enhanced Eventstream
fabricroadmap.summary: The Eventstream homepage makes it even easier to bring in data. By clicking on the “Add external source”, you will find these sources in the Get events wizard that helps you to set up the source in a few steps. After you add the source to your eventstream, you can publish it to stream the data into your eventstream. Using Eventstream with discrete sources to turn events into streams for more analysis. You can send the streams to different Fabric data destinations, like Lakehouse and KQL Database.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream Edit and Live modes
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream offers two distinct modes, Edit and Live, to provide flexibility and control over the development process of your eventstream. If you create a new Eventstream with Enhanced Capabilities enabled, you can modify it in an Edit mode. Here, you can design stream processing operations for your data streams using a no-code editor. Once you complete the editing, you can publish your Eventstream and visualize how it starts streaming and processing data in Live mode.

fabricroadmap.title: Default and Derived Streams
fabricroadmap.summary: Multiple streams are listed within the Real-Time Hub including Default and Derived streams. Default stream are automatically generated when a streaming source is added to Eventstream. Default stream captures raw event data directly from the source, ready for transformation or analysis. erived stream: A specialized stream that users can create as a destination within Eventstream. Derived stream can be created after a series of operations such as filtering and aggregating, and then it’s ready for further consumption or analysis by other users in the organization through the Real-Time Hub.

fabricroadmap.title: New streaming connectors for Kafka public clusters and more instances of SQL Server DB CDC
fabricroadmap.summary: Additional connectors will be available through the Get Events experience, including Public Kafka clusters and SQL Server DB CDC.

fabricroadmap.title: Additional Fabric system events
fabricroadmap.summary: More Fabric Event categories will be available for use in Real-Time hub, namely Fabric Job events, OneLake events

fabricroadmap.title: Schema Registry in Eventstream Public Preview
fabricroadmap.summary: Schema Registry in Fabric Real-Time Intelligence provides centralized schema management to enforce data quality, enable schema validation, and simplify integration across streaming data pipelines.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream integration with Managed Private Endpoint
fabricroadmap.summary: This integration with Managed Private Endpoints enables secure and private access to data sources behind a firewall or blocked from public internet access, allowing data to be streamed to Fabric Eventstream over outbound connections.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse destination support Eventstreams
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstreams will add support for Eventhouse as a destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Set Alert on Real-Time Dashboards
fabricroadmap.summary: In addition to monitoring Power BI and Eventstream data, Data Activator will support periodic querying against KQL queries saved in Real-Time Dashboards. These queries can be used to return exceptions, or track results over time to detect data changes or threshold conditions.

fabricroadmap.title: Enhanced trigger options
fabricroadmap.summary: To represent the business conditions for monitoring, Data Activator will support more trigger conditions such as percentage changes over time, date/time functions, basic mathematic functions, signal absence detection and more.

fabricroadmap.title: Pro-Code support for CRUD for Functions/MV/Update policies
fabricroadmap.summary: The new Pro-Code CRUD experience for Functions empowers developers to create, read, update, and delete Kusto Functions and Materialized Views through a streamlined, code-first interface. It eliminates the need to memorize command syntax, . This enhancement is designed to accelerate productivity while preserving full control for experienced users.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventhouse Minimum Capacity Adjustments
fabricroadmap.summary: The "Min Consumption" button has evolved into two distinct features for greater clarity and control. Always On, now enabled by default, ensures continuous availability without incurring premium storage costs, while Minimum Consumption allows you to define a baseline compute level, optimizing for both performance and cost. This change enhances transparency and empowers smarter resource management.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream supports customers to upload own connector
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables customers to develop or reuse their own Kafka connectors, or open-source Kafka connectors, when no pre-built streaming connector is available.With this capability, you can:- Customize your own connector at your own pace.- Run with no infrastructure to manage.- Reuse open-source connectors directly.

fabricroadmap.title: Send alerts to Teams groups and channels
fabricroadmap.summary: Users can set up rules that send alerts to Teams groups and channels.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream integration with Cribl as source
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature provides a dedicated source in Real-Time Hub for Cribl, making it easy for customers to integrate with Cribl.

fabricroadmap.title: Support SSL encryption for Eventstream connector data transmission
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allows customers to specify their own certificate for SSL encryption, enabling secure data transmission between the Eventstream streaming connector client and their source servers, such as Apache Kafka or MQTT.

fabricroadmap.title: Workspace level private link
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature is to provide workspace level network isolation for incoming connections. When customer enables workspace level private link, they can configure the connections to the specific workspace from certain Virtual network while blocking connections from other VNet or public internet.

fabricroadmap.title: Simplified Rule and Object Creation Experience
fabricroadmap.summary: This intuitive and streamlined experience allows you to create rules at the desired level of data tracking. Whether you wish to monitor data at the event level or object level, you now have the flexibility to do so as you build your rule.

fabricroadmap.title: KQL Database Entity Diagram – show functions, materialized views, update policies, and more
fabricroadmap.summary: a visual representation of the KQL database entities and their relations (such as tables, functions, materialized views, and more).

fabricroadmap.title: Evenhouse table no-code creation and editing experience
fabricroadmap.summary: Wizards to create/edit tables

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream Integrated Activator Alert Setup Experience
fabricroadmap.summary: The new Activator Alert feature in Eventstream allows users to set up alerts in a single step, streamlining the process. With this enhancement, customers can quickly create alerts directly within Eventstream, saving time and reducing complexity.

fabricroadmap.title: UX for viewing Eventhouse functions
fabricroadmap.summary: Public Preview: Q1 2026

fabricroadmap.title: Lakehouse Streaming Tables in the Real Time hub
fabricroadmap.summary: Lakehouse Streaming Tables bring real-time data processing and analytics to the Fabric Real Time hub, making it easier for data engineers and data scientists to discover, explore, and act on streaming data - all in one central location. With seamless integration to Spark and AI Skills, users can filter, open, and endorse streaming tables, and launch advanced analytics experiences.
